1: # OpenCode ECC Plugin
2: 
3: > WARNING: This README is specific to OpenCode usage.
4: > If you installed ECC via npm (e.g. `npm install opencode-ecc`), refer to the root README instead.
5: 
6: ECC plugin for OpenCode - agents, commands, hooks, and skills.
7: 
8: ## Installation
9: 
10: ## Installation Overview
11: 
12: There are two ways to use ECC:
13: 
14: 1. **npm package (recommended for most users)**
15:    Install via npm/bun/yarn and use the `ecc-install` CLI to set up rules and agents.
16: 
17: 2. **Direct clone / plugin mode**
18:    Clone the repository and run OpenCode directly inside it.
19: 
20: Choose the method that matches your workflow below.
21: 
22: ### Option 1: npm Package
23: 
24: ```bash
25: npm install ecc-universal
26: ```
27: 
28: Add to your `opencode.json`:
29: 
30: ```json
31: {
32:   "plugin": ["ecc-universal"]
33: }
34: ```
35: 
36: This loads the ECC OpenCode plugin module from npm:
37: - hook/event integrations
38: - bundled custom tools exported by the plugin
39: 
40: It does **not** auto-register the full ECC command/agent/instruction catalog in your project config. For the full OpenCode setup, either:
41: - run OpenCode inside this repository, or
42: - copy the relevant `.opencode/commands/`, `.opencode/prompts/`, `.opencode/instructions/`, and the `instructions`, `agent`, and `command` config entries into your own project
43: 
44: After installation, the `ecc-install` CLI is also available:
45: 
46: ```bash
47: npx ecc-install typescript
48: ```
49: 
50: ### Option 2: Direct Use
51: 
52: Clone and run OpenCode in the repository:
53: 
54: ```bash
55: git clone https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC
56: cd ECC
57: opencode
58: ```
59: 
60: If you also want to apply the ECC home install
61: (`node scripts/install-apply.js --target opencode --profile full`), build the
62: plugin first so the compiled payload at `.opencode/dist/` exists:
63: 
64: ```bash
65: node scripts/build-opencode.js   # or: npm run build:opencode
66: node scripts/install-apply.js --target opencode --profile full
67: ```
68: 
69: Without `.opencode/dist/index.js`, OpenCode will detect the slash commands
70: but silently skip plugin hooks and tools. The installer now fails fast with
71: a pointer to this command if the build step is missing.
72:

1: # Migration Guide: Claude Code to OpenCode
2: 
3: This guide helps you migrate from Claude Code to OpenCode while using the ECC configuration.
4: 
5: ## Overview
6: 
7: OpenCode is an alternative CLI for AI-assisted development that supports **all** the same features as Claude Code, with some differences in configuration format.
8: 
9: ## Key Differences
10: 
11: | Feature | Claude Code | OpenCode | Notes |
12: |---------|-------------|----------|-------|
13: | Configuration | `CLAUDE.md`, `plugin.json` | `opencode.json` | Different file formats |
14: | Agents | Markdown frontmatter | JSON object | Full parity |
15: | Commands | `commands/*.md` | `command` object or `.md` files | Full parity |
16: | Skills | `skills/*/SKILL.md` | `instructions` array | Loaded as context |
17: | **Hooks** | `hooks.json` (3 phases) | **Plugin system (20+ events)** | **Full parity + more!** |
18: | Rules | `rules/*.md` | `instructions` array | Consolidated or separate |
19: | MCP | Full support | Full support | Full parity |
20: 
21: ## Hook Migration
22: 
23: **OpenCode fully supports hooks** via its plugin system, which is actually MORE sophisticated than Claude Code with 20+ event types.
24: 
25: ### Hook Event Mapping
26: 
27: | Claude Code Hook | OpenCode Plugin Event | Notes |
28: |-----------------|----------------------|-------|
29: | `PreToolUse` | `tool.execute.before` | Can modify tool input |
30: | `PostToolUse` | `tool.execute.after` | Can modify tool output |
31: | `Stop` | `session.idle` or `session.status` | Session lifecycle |
32: | `SessionStart` | `session.created` | Session begins |
33: | `SessionEnd` | `session.deleted` | Session ends |
34: | N/A | `file.edited` | OpenCode-only: file changes |
35: | N/A | `file.watcher.updated` | OpenCode-only: file system watch |
36: | N/A | `message.updated` | OpenCode-only: message changes |
37: | N/A | `lsp.client.diagnostics` | OpenCode-only: LSP integration |
38: | N/A | `tui.toast.show` | OpenCode-only: notifications |
39: 
40: ### Converting Hooks to Plugins
41: 
42: **Claude Code hook (hooks.json):**
43: ```json
44: {
45:   "PostToolUse": [{
46:     "matcher": "tool == \"Edit\" && tool_input.file_path matches \"\\\\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx)$\"",
47:     "hooks": [{
48:       "type": "command",
49:       "command": "prettier --write \"$file_path\""
50:     }]
51:   }]
52: }
53: ```
54: 
55: **OpenCode plugin (.opencode/plugins/prettier-hook.ts):**
56: ```typescript
57: export const PrettierPlugin = async ({ $ }) => {
58:   return {
59:     "file.edited": async (event) => {
60:       if (event.path.match(/\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx)$/)) {
61:         await $`prettier --write ${event.path}`
62:       }
63:     }

281: ## Plugin Installation
282: 
283: ### Option 1: Use ECC Configuration Directly
284: 
285: The `.opencode/` directory contains everything pre-configured.
286: 
287: ### Option 2: Install as npm Package
288: 
289: ```bash
290: npm install ecc-universal
291: ```
292: 
293: Then in your `opencode.json`:
294: ```json
295: {
296:   "plugin": ["ecc-universal"]
297: }
298: ```
299: 
300: This only loads the published ECC OpenCode plugin module (hooks/events and exported plugin tools).
301: It does **not** automatically inject ECC's full `agent`, `command`, or `instructions` config into your project.
302: 
303: If you want the full ECC OpenCode workflow surface, use the repository's bundled `.opencode/opencode.json` as your base config or copy these pieces into your project:
304: - `.opencode/commands/`
305: - `.opencode/prompts/`
306: - `.opencode/instructions/INSTRUCTIONS.md`
307: - the `agent` and `command` sections from `.opencode/opencode.json`
308: 
309: ## Troubleshooting
310: 
311: ### Configuration Not Loading
312: 
313: 1. Verify `.opencode/opencode.json` exists in the repository root
314: 2. Check JSON syntax is valid: `cat .opencode/opencode.json | jq .`
315: 3. Ensure all referenced prompt files exist
316: 
317: ### Plugin Not Loading
318: 
319: 1. Verify plugin file exists in `.opencode/plugins/`
320: 2. Check TypeScript syntax is valid
321: 3. Ensure `plugin` array in `opencode.json` includes the path
322: 
323: ### Agent Not Found
324: 
325: 1. Check the agent is defined in `opencode.json` under the `agent` object
326: 2. Verify the prompt file path is correct
327: 3. Ensure the prompt file exists at the specified path
328: 
329: ### Command Not Working
330: 
331: 1. Verify the command is defined in `opencode.json` or as `.md` file in `.opencode/commands/`
332: 2. Check the referenced agent exists
333: 3. Ensure the template uses `$ARGUMENTS` for user input
334: 4. If you installed only `plugin: ["ecc-universal"]`, note that npm plugin install does not auto-add ECC commands or agents to your project config
335: 
336: ## Best Practices
337: 
338: 1. **Start Fresh**: Don't try to run both Claude Code and OpenCode simultaneously
339: 2. **Check Configuration**: Verify `opencode.json` loads without errors
340: 3. **Test Commands**: Run each command once to verify it works
341: 4. **Use Plugins**: Leverage the plugin hooks for automation
342: 5. **Use Agents**: Leverage the specialized agents for their intended purposes
343: 
344: ## Reverting to Claude Code
345: 
346: If you need to switch back:
347: 
348: 1. Simply run `claude` instead of `opencode`
349: 2. Claude Code will use its own configuration (`CLAUDE.md`, `plugin.json`, etc.)
350: 3. The `.opencode/` directory won't interfere with Claude Code

1: # 🧠🦾🦿 Arquitetura Corporal do OpenCode
2: 
3: > "OpenCode é a cabeça, Tesseract são os olhos, agents/subagents/skills/MCP são o tronco, braços e pernas."
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 🧠 CABEÇA — OpenCode (Orquestrador Central)
8: 
9: A **cabeça** é o OpenCode — o cérebro que pensa, decide e coordena tudo.
10: 
11: | Componente | Função |
12: |------------|--------|
13: | **Modelo LLM** | Raciocínio, planejamento, tomada de decisão |
14: | **Contexto** | Memória de curto prazo (janela de contexto) |
15: | **CLAUDE.md** | Preferências globais e regras comportamentais |
16: | **Skills** | Conhecimento especializado carregado sob demanda |
17: | **Hooks** | Gatilhos automáticos (pré/pós ação) |
18: 
19: ### Centros de Comando (Cabeça)
20: ```
21: opencode.json          → Configuração neural central
22: CLAUDE.md              → Personalidade e regras
23: ~/.opencode/skills/    → Memória de procedimentos
24: ~/.opencode/hooks/     → Reflexos automáticos
25: ```
26: 
27: ### Fluxo de Pensamento
28: ```
29: Usuário pede → OpenCode analisa → Escolhe skill/agent → Delega → Sintetiza resultado
30:      ↑                                                            ↓
31:      └────────────────── Feedback loop ──────────────────────────┘
32: ```
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 👁️👁️ OLHOS — Tesseract OCR + Pipelines de Visão
37: 
38: Os **olhos** enxergam o mundo — extraem texto de PDFs, imagens, documentos e sites.
39: 
40: | Componente | Função |
41: |------------|--------|
42: | **Tesseract 5.5.2** | Motor OCR (PT + EN) |
43: | **pdftotext** | Extração de texto de PDFs digitais |
44: | **Text Extractor** | Plugin OCR dentro do Obsidian |
45: | **OCR Pipeline** | Script `ocr_extract.py` — processamento em lote |
46: | **webfetch/websearch** | "Olhar" para a internet |
47: 
48: ### Hierarquia Visual
49: ```
50: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
51: │              OLHOS DO OPENCODE              │
52: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
53: │                                             │
54: │  👁️ Visão Próxima (Local)                   │
55: │  ├── Tesseract OCR → imagens, PDFs escaneados│
56: │  ├── pdftotext → PDFs com texto digital     │
57: │  ├── Pillow → manipulação de imagens        │
58: │  └── OCR Pipeline → processamento em lote   │
59: │                                             │
60: │  👁️ Visão Distante (Rede)                   │
61: │  ├── webfetch → páginas web                 │
62: │  ├── websearch → busca semântica            │
63: │  ├── agent-reach → 15 plataformas           │
64: │  └── Playwright → navegação browser         │
65: │                                             │
66: │  👁️ Visão Técnica (Código)                  │
67: │  ├── GhidraMCP → engenharia reversa         │
68: │  ├── LSP → análise de código                │
69: │  ├── Graphify → grafo de conhecimento       │
70: │  └── Codegraph → indexação semântica        │
71: │                                             │
72: └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
73: ```
74: 
75: ### Comandos dos Olhos
76: ```bash
77: # Extração de texto
78: ocr file /caminho/arquivo.pdf     # Olhar para um arquivo
79: ocr search "termo"                # Buscar nas extrações
80: ocr rebuild                       # Reescanear tudo
81: 
82: # Visão web
83: webfetch <url>                    # Olhar para uma página
84: websearch <query>                 # Buscar na internet
85: ```
86: 
87: ---
88: 
89: ## 🦴 TRONCO — Agents e Subagents (Estrutura Central)
90: 
91: O **tronco** sustenta tudo — são os agents que executam o trabalho pesado.
92: 
93: ### Hierarquia de Agents
94: ```
95: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
96: │                   TRONCO                        │
97: │              (Agents Principais)                │
98: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
99: │                                                 │
100: │  🧠 AGENTS DE PENSAMENTO                        │
101: │  ├── oracle      → Consultor High-IQ            │
102: │  ├── planner     → Planejador especialista      │
103: │  ├── architect   → Arquiteto de sistemas        │
104: │  └── explore     → Explorador de código         │
105: │                                                 │
106: │  🔧 AGENTS DE EXECUÇÃO                          │
107: │  ├── build       → Desenvolvedor principal      │
108: │  ├── code-reviewer → Revisor de código          │
109: │  ├── security-reviewer → Auditoria de segurança │
110: │  ├── python-reviewer → Especialista Python      │
111: │  ├── rust-reviewer → Especialista Rust          │
112: │  └── tdd-guide   → Especialista TDD             │
113: │                                                 │
114: │  📚 AGENTS DE CONHECIMENTO                      │
115: │  ├── librarian   → Busca documentação           │
116: │  ├── docs-lookup → Consulta APIs                │
117: │  ├── doc-updater → Atualiza documentação        │
118: │  └── multimodal-looker → Análise de mídia      │
119: │                                                 │
120: │  🔍 AGENTS ESPECIALIZADOS                       │
121: │  ├── reverser    → Engenharia reversa (Ghidra)  │
122: │  ├── memory-keeper → Memória persistente        │
123: │  ├── loop-operator → Operador de loops          │
124: │  └── gsd-*       → Sistema GSD completo         │
125: │                                                 │
126: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
127: ```
128: 
129: ### Subagents (Braços de Trabalho)
130: ```
131: Sisyphus-Junior    → Executor focado (sem delegar)
132: Sisyphus (deep)    → Problemas complexos autônomos
133: Sisyphus (quick)   → Tarefas triviais rápidas
134: ```
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## 💪 BRAÇOS — Skills (Habilidades Especializadas)
139: 
140: Os **braços** são as skills — cada uma é uma habilidade que o OpenCode pode "usar" para executar tarefas específicas.
141: 
142: ### Mapa de Skills por Domínio
143: ```
144: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
145: │                    BRAÇOS (SKILLS)                       │
146: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
147: │                                                         │
148: │  🖥️ DESENVOLVIMENTO                                     │
149: │  ├── shared/programming     → Python, Rust, TS, Go      │
150: │  ├── tdd-workflow           → Test-Driven Development   │
151: │  ├── error-handling         → Padrões de erro           │
152: │  ├── git-workflow           → Fluxo Git                 │
153: │  └── e2e-testing            → Testes E2E                │
154: │                                                         │
155: │  🎨 INTERFACE                                           │
156: │  ├── ui-styling             → shadcn/ui + Tailwind      │
157: │  ├── ui-ux-pro-max          → Design UI/UX              │
158: │  ├── frontend-design        → Design frontend           │
159: │  ├── banner-design          → Banners e assets          │
160: │  └── slides                 → Apresentações             │
161: │                                                         │
162: │  🔐 SEGURANÇA                                           │
163: │  ├── security-research      → Caça-falhas (3+2 agents)  │
164: │  ├── production-audit       → Auditoria local           │
165: │  └── security-review        → Revisão de código         │
166: │                                                         │
167: │  🔧 HARDWARE                                            │
168: │  ├── electronics-debug      → PCB, SMPS, microsolda     │
169: │  ├── firmware-reverse       → BIOS, firmware, binário   │
170: │  ├── hardware-intelligence  → GPU MI50, inferência      │
171: │  └── ghidra-re-pipeline     → Pipeline RE completo      │
172: │                                                         │
173: │  🧠 CONHECIMENTO                                        │
174: │  ├── cerebral-wikia         → Wiki persistente LLM      │
175: │  ├── graphify               → Grafo de conhecimento     │
176: │  ├── ck                     → Memória por projeto       │
177: │  └── intelecto-compartilhado → Cérebro compartilhado   │
178: │                                                         │
179: │  📋 GESTÃO                                              │
180: │  ├── gran-mestre            → Orquestrador meta         │
181: │  ├── gsd-* (50+ skills)     → Sistema GSD completo      │
182: │  ├── codebase-onboarding    → Onboarding de projeto     │
183: │  └── architecture-decision-records → ADRs               │
184: │                                                         │
185: │  🔍 PESQUISA                                            │
186: │  ├── agent-reach            → 15 plataformas web        │
187: │  ├── shared/ulw-research    → Pesquisa ultra profunda   │
188: │  └── shared/ultimate-browsing → Acesso a sites bloqueados│
189: │                                                         │
190: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
191: ```
192: 
193: ---
194: 
195: ## 🦵 PERNAS — MCPs e Integrações Externas
196: 
197: As **pernas** são os MCPs (Model Context Protocol) — conectam o OpenCode ao mundo exterior.
198: 
199: ### MCPs Ativos
200: ```
201: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
202: │                    PERNAS (MCPs)                         │
203: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
204: │                                                         │
205: │  🌐 CONEXÃO COM O MUNDO                                 │
206: │  ├── GhidraMCP (127.0.0.1:8080) → Engenharia reversa   │
207: │  ├── Context7     → Documentação atualizada de libs     │
208: │  ├── Codegraph    → Grafo semântico do código           │
209: │  └── Playwright   → Navegação web automatizada          │
210: │                                                         │
211: │  📁 SISTEMAS LOCAIS                                     │
212: │  ├── Obsidian Vault → /mnt/dados/cerebro com IA/        │
213: │  ├── OCR Pipeline  → ~/.opencode/scripts/ocr-pipeline/  │
214: │  ├── Cérebro       → /mnt/dados/cerebro com IA/wiki/    │
215: │  └── BIOS Modding  → /mnt/dados/projetos/bios modding/  │
216: │                                                         │
217: │  🔧 FERRAMENTAS EXTERNAS                                │
218: │  ├── EZP2019 (scriba) → Programador EEPROM              │
219: │  ├── Tesseract OCR    → Visão computacional              │
220: │  ├── pdftotext        → Extração de PDFs                 │
221: │  └── Git              → Controle de versão               │
222: │                                                         │
223: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
224: ```
225: 
226: ---
227: 
228: ## 🔄 INTEGRAÇÃO — Como o Corpo Funciona Junto
229: 
230: ### Fluxo Típico: "Extrair texto de um PDF e contextualizar"
231: 
232: ```
233: 1. 🧠 CABEÇA (OpenCode) recebe pedido
234:    └─ "Analise o datasheet do LM217"
235: 
236: 2. 👁️ OLHOS (Tesseract/pdftotext) examinam o PDF
237:    └─ extrai 59.733 caracteres de texto
238: 
239: 3. 🦴 TRONCO (Agent build/oracle) processa
240:    └─ Analisa parâmetros elétricos, pinagem, aplicações
241: 
242: 4. 💪 BRAÇOS (Skills) executam
243:    └─ firmware-reverse analisa se é relevante para BIOS
244:    └─ electronics-debug verifica compatibilidade
245: 
246: 5. 🦵 PERNAS (MCPs) persistem
247:    └─ Obsidian recebe nota atualizada com texto extraído
248:    └─ Cérebro armazena conhecimento para futuras sessões
249: 
250: 6. 🧠 CABEÇA sintetiza e responde ao usuário
251: ```
252: 
253: ### Mapa de Conexões
254: ```
255:                     ┌──────────────┐
256:                     │   🧠 OPENCODE │
257:                     │   (Cabeça)    │
258:                     └──────┬───────┘
259:                            │
260:             ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
261:             │              │              │
262:        ┌────▼────┐   ┌────▼────┐   ┌────▼────┐
263:        │ 👁️👁️ OCR │   │ 🦴 AGENTS│   │ 💪 SKILLS│
264:        │ (Olhos)  │   │ (Tronco) │   │ (Braços) │
265:        └────┬────┘   └────┬────┘   └────┬────┘
266:             │              │              │
267:             └──────────────┼──────────────┘
268:                            │
269:                     ┌──────▼───────┐
270:                     │  🦵 MCPs/EXT  │
271:                     │  (Pernas)     │
272:                     └──────────────┘
273: ```
274: 
275: ---
276: 
277: ## 📊 Inventário do Corpo
278: 
279: | Parte | Componentes | Quantidade |
280: |-------|-------------|------------|
281: | 🧠 Cabeça | OpenCode + Config | 1 |
282: | 👁️ Olhos | Tesseract + pdftotext + web tools | 5 motores |
283: | 🦴 Tronco | Agents principais | 20+ agents |
284: | 💪 Braços | Skills especializadas | 100+ skills |
285: | 🦵 Pernas | MCPs + Integrações | 10+ conexões |
286: 
287: ---
288: 
289: ## 🎯 Princípios da Arquitetura
290: 
291: 1. **Olhos antes de agir** — Sempre extrair e entender antes de processar
292: 2. **Cabeça delega, não executa** — OpenCode coordena, agents fazem
293: 3. **Braços especializados** — Cada skill é um especialista
294: 4. **Pernas conectam** — MCPs são a ponte com o mundo
295: 5. **Memória compartilhada** — Cérebro (Obsidian) alimenta todos
296: 
297: ---

1: # Hooks
2: 
3: Hooks are event-driven automations that fire before or after Claude Code tool executions. They enforce code quality, catch mistakes early, and automate repetitive checks.
4: 
5: ## How Hooks Work
6: 
7: ```
8: User request → Claude picks a tool → PreToolUse hook runs → Tool executes → PostToolUse hook runs
9: ```
10: 
11: - **PreToolUse** hooks run before the tool executes. They can **block** (exit code 2) or **warn** (stderr without blocking).
12: - **PostToolUse** hooks run after the tool completes. They can analyze output but cannot block.
13: - **Stop** hooks run after each Claude response.
14: - **SessionStart/SessionEnd** hooks run at session lifecycle boundaries.
15: - **PreCompact** hooks run before context compaction, useful for saving state.
16: 
17: ## Hooks in This Plugin
18: 
19: Memory persistence lifecycle definitions live in `hooks/memory-persistence/`.
20: The executable hook graph remains `hooks/hooks.json`; the memory persistence directory is the stable contract for SessionStart, PreCompact, observation, activity tracking, and SessionEnd behavior.
21: 
22: ## Installing These Hooks Manually
23: 
24: For Claude Code manual installs, do not paste the raw repo `hooks.json` into `~/.claude/settings.json` or copy it directly into `~/.claude/hooks/hooks.json`. The checked-in file is plugin/repo-oriented and is meant to be installed through the ECC installer or loaded as a plugin.
25: 
26: Use the installer instead so hook commands are rewritten against your actual Claude root:
27: 
28: ```bash
29: bash ./install.sh --target claude --modules hooks-runtime
30: ```
31: 
32: ```powershell
33: pwsh -File .\install.ps1 --target claude --modules hooks-runtime
34: ```
35: 
36: That installs resolved hooks to `~/.claude/hooks/hooks.json`. On Windows, the Claude config root is `%USERPROFILE%\\.claude`.
37: 
38: ### PreToolUse Hooks
39: 
40: | Hook | Matcher | Behavior | Exit Code |
41: |------|---------|----------|-----------|
42: | **Dev server blocker** | `Bash` | Blocks `npm run dev` etc. outside tmux — ensures log access | 2 (blocks) |
43: | **Tmux reminder** | `Bash` | Suggests tmux for long-running commands (npm test, cargo build, docker) | 0 (warns) |
44: | **Git push reminder** | `Bash` | Reminds to review changes before `git push` | 0 (warns) |
45: | **Pre-commit quality check** | `Bash` | Runs quality checks before `git commit`: lints staged files, validates commit message format when provided via `-m/--message`, detects console.log/debugger/secrets | 2 (blocks critical) / 0 (warns) |
46: | **Doc file warning** | `Write` | Warns about non-standard `.md`/`.txt` files (allows README, CLAUDE, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, LICENSE, SKILL, docs/, skills/); cross-platform path handling | 0 (warns) |
47: | **Strategic compact** | `Edit\|Write` | Suggests manual `/compact` at logical intervals (every ~50 tool calls) | 0 (warns) |
48: 
49: ### PostToolUse Hooks
50: 
51: | Hook | Matcher | What It Does |
52: |------|---------|-------------|
53: | **PR logger** | `Bash` | Logs PR URL and review command after `gh pr create` |
54: | **Build analysis** | `Bash` | Background analysis after build commands (async, non-blocking) |
55: | **Quality gate** | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | Runs fast quality checks after edits |
56: | **Design quality check** | `Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit` | Warns when frontend edits drift toward generic template-looking UI |
57: | **Prettier format** | `Edit` | Auto-formats JS/TS files with Prettier after edits |
58: | **TypeScript check** | `Edit` | Runs `tsc --noEmit` after editing `.ts`/`.tsx` files |
59: | **console.log warning** | `Edit` | Warns about `console.log` statements in edited files |
60: 
61: ### Lifecycle Hooks
62: 
63: | Hook | Event | What It Does |
64: |------|-------|-------------|
65: | **Session start** | `SessionStart` | Loads previous context and detects package manager |
66: | **Plan Canvas sessions** | `SessionStart` | Surfaces open Plan Canvas browser reviews so a fresh session can resume the loop |
67: | **Pre-compact** | `PreCompact` | Saves state before context compaction |
68: | **Console.log audit** | `Stop` | Checks all modified files for `console.log` after each response |
69: | **Session summary** | `Stop` | Persists session state when transcript path is available |
70: | **Pattern extraction** | `Stop` | Evaluates session for extractable patterns (continuous learning) |
71: | **Cost tracker** | `Stop` | Emits lightweight run-cost telemetry markers |
72: | **Desktop notify** | `Stop` | Sends macOS desktop notification with task summary (standard+) |
73: | **Session end marker** | `SessionEnd` | Lifecycle marker and cleanup log |
74: 
75: ## Customizing Hooks
76: 
77: ### Disabling a Hook
78: 
79: Remove or comment out the hook entry in `hooks.json`. If installed as a plugin, override in your `~/.claude/settings.json`:
80: 
81: ```json
82: {
83:   "hooks": {
84:     "PreToolUse": [
85:       {
86:         "matcher": "Write",
87:         "hooks": [],
88:         "description": "Override: allow all .md file creation"
89:       }
90:     ]
91:   }
92: }
93: ```
94: 
95: ### Runtime Hook Controls (Recommended)
96: 
97: Use environment variables to control hook behavior without editing `hooks.json`:
98: 
99: ```bash
100: # minimal | standard | strict (default: standard)
101: export ECC_HOOK_PROFILE=standard
102: 
103: # Disable specific hook IDs (comma-separated)
104: export ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS="pre:bash:tmux-reminder,post:edit:typecheck"
105: 
106: # Disable only GateGuard during setup or recovery
107: export ECC_GATEGUARD=off
108: 
109: # Cap SessionStart additional context (default: 8000 chars)
110: export ECC_SESSION_START_MAX_CHARS=4000
111: 
112: # Disable SessionStart additional context entirely
113: export ECC_SESSION_START_CONTEXT=off

116: export ECC_CONTEXT_MONITOR_COST_WARNINGS=off
117: ```
118: 
119: Windows PowerShell:
120: 
121: ```powershell
122: [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('ECC_CONTEXT_MONITOR_COST_WARNINGS', 'off', 'User')
123: ```
124: 
125: Profiles:
126: - `minimal` — keep essential lifecycle and safety hooks only.
127: - `standard` — default; balanced quality + safety checks.
128: - `strict` — enables additional reminders and stricter guardrails.
129: 
130: ### Writing Your Own Hook
131: 
132: Hooks are shell commands that receive tool input as JSON on stdin and must output JSON on stdout.
133: 
134: **Basic structure:**
135: 
136: ```javascript
137: // my-hook.js
138: let data = '';
139: process.stdin.on('data', chunk => data += chunk);
140: process.stdin.on('end', () => {
141:   const input = JSON.parse(data);
142: 
143:   // Access tool info
144:   const toolName = input.tool_name;        // "Edit", "Bash", "Write", etc.
145:   const toolInput = input.tool_input;      // Tool-specific parameters
146:   const toolOutput = input.tool_output;    // Only available in PostToolUse
147: 
148:   // Warn (non-blocking): write to stderr
149:   console.error('[Hook] Warning message shown to Claude');
150: 
151:   // Block (PreToolUse only): exit with code 2
152:   // process.exit(2);
153: 
154:   // Always output the original data to stdout
155:   console.log(data);
156: });
157: ```
158: 
159: **Exit codes:**
160: - `0` — Success (continue execution)
161: - `2` — Block the tool call (PreToolUse only)
162: - Other non-zero — Error (logged but does not block)
163: 
164: ### Hook Input Schema
165: 
166: ```typescript
167: interface HookInput {
168:   tool_name: string;          // "Bash", "Edit", "Write", "Read", etc.
169:   tool_input: {
170:     command?: string;         // Bash: the command being run
171:     file_path?: string;       // Edit/Write/Read: target file
172:     old_string?: string;      // Edit: text being replaced
173:     new_string?: string;      // Edit: replacement text
174:     content?: string;         // Write: file content
175:   };
176:   tool_output?: {             // PostToolUse only
177:     output?: string;          // Command/tool output
178:   };
179: }
180: ```
181: 
182: ### Async Hooks
183: 
184: For hooks that should not block the main flow (e.g., background analysis):
185: 
186: ```json
187: {
188:   "type": "command",
189:   "command": "node my-slow-hook.js",
190:   "async": true,
191:   "timeout": 30
192: }
193: ```
194: 
195: Async hooks run in the background. They cannot block tool execution.
196: 
197: ## Common Hook Recipes
198: 
199: ### Warn about TODO comments
200: 
201: ```json
202: {
203:   "matcher": "Edit",
204:   "hooks": [{
205:     "type": "command",
206:     "command": "node -e \"let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{const i=JSON.parse(d);const ns=i.tool_input?.new_string||'';if(/TODO|FIXME|HACK/.test(ns)){console.error('[Hook] New TODO/FIXME added - consider creating an issue')}console.log(d)})\""
207:   }],
208:   "description": "Warn when adding TODO/FIXME comments"
209: }
210: ```
211: 
212: ### Block large file creation
213: 
214: ```json
215: {
216:   "matcher": "Write",
217:   "hooks": [{
218:     "type": "command",
219:     "command": "node -e \"let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{const i=JSON.parse(d);const c=i.tool_input?.content||'';const lines=c.split('\\n').length;if(lines>800){console.error('[Hook] BLOCKED: File exceeds 800 lines ('+lines+' lines)');console.error('[Hook] Split into smaller, focused modules');process.exit(2)}console.log(d)})\""
220:   }],
221:   "description": "Block creation of files larger than 800 lines"
222: }
223: ```
224: 
225: ### Auto-format Python files with ruff
226: 
227: ```json
228: {
229:   "matcher": "Edit",
230:   "hooks": [{
231:     "type": "command",
232:     "command": "node -e \"let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{const i=JSON.parse(d);const p=i.tool_input?.file_path||'';if(/\\.py$/.test(p)){const{execFileSync}=require('child_process');try{execFileSync('ruff',['format',p],{stdio:'pipe'})}catch(e){}}console.log(d)})\""
233:   }],
234:   "description": "Auto-format Python files with ruff after edits"
235: }
236: ```
237: 
238: ### Require test files alongside new source files
239: 
240: ```json
241: {
242:   "matcher": "Write",
243:   "hooks": [{
244:     "type": "command",
245:     "command": "node -e \"const fs=require('fs');let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{const i=JSON.parse(d);const p=i.tool_input?.file_path||'';if(/src\\/.*\\.(ts|js)$/.test(p)&&!/\\.test\\.|\\.spec\\./.test(p)){const testPath=p.replace(/\\.(ts|js)$/,'.test.$1');if(!fs.existsSync(testPath)){console.error('[Hook] No test file found for: '+p);console.error('[Hook] Expected: '+testPath);console.error('[Hook] Consider writing tests first (/tdd)')}}console.log(d)})\""
246:   }],
247:   "description": "Remind to create tests when adding new source files"
248: }
249: ```

252:

1: # ECC - OpenCode Instructions
2: 
3: This document consolidates the core rules and guidelines from the Claude Code configuration for use with OpenCode.
4: 
5: ## Security Guidelines (CRITICAL)
6: 
7: ### Mandatory Security Checks
8: 
9: Before ANY commit:
10: - [ ] No hardcoded secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)
11: - [ ] All user inputs validated
12: - [ ] SQL injection prevention (parameterized queries)
13: - [ ] XSS prevention (sanitized HTML)
14: - [ ] CSRF protection enabled
15: - [ ] Authentication/authorization verified
16: - [ ] Rate limiting on all endpoints
17: - [ ] Error messages don't leak sensitive data
18: 
19: ### Secret Management
20: 
21: ```typescript
22: // NEVER: Hardcoded secrets
23: const apiKey = "sk-proj-xxxxx"
24: 
25: // ALWAYS: Environment variables
26: const apiKey = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY
27: 
28: if (!apiKey) {
29:   throw new Error('OPENAI_API_KEY not configured')
30: }
31: ```
32: 
33: ### Security Response Protocol
34: 
35: If security issue found:
36: 1. STOP immediately
37: 2. Use **security-reviewer** agent
38: 3. Fix CRITICAL issues before continuing
39: 4. Rotate any exposed secrets
40: 5. Review entire codebase for similar issues
41: 
42: ---
43: 
44: ## Coding Style
45: 
46: ### Immutability (CRITICAL)
47: 
48: ALWAYS create new objects, NEVER mutate:
49: 
50: ```javascript
51: // WRONG: Mutation
52: function updateUser(user, name) {
53:   user.name = name  // MUTATION!
54:   return user
55: }
56: 
57: // CORRECT: Immutability
58: function updateUser(user, name) {
59:   return {
60:     ...user,
61:     name
62:   }
63: }
64: ```
65: 
66: ### File Organization
67: 
68: MANY SMALL FILES > FEW LARGE FILES:
69: - High cohesion, low coupling
70: - 200-400 lines typical, 800 max
71: - Extract utilities from large components
72: - Organize by feature/domain, not by type
73: 
74: ### Error Handling
75: 
76: ALWAYS handle errors comprehensively:
77: 
78: ```typescript
79: try {
80:   const result = await riskyOperation()
81:   return result
82: } catch (error) {
83:   console.error('Operation failed:', error)
84:   throw new Error('Detailed user-friendly message')
85: }
86: ```
87: 
88: ### Input Validation
89: 
90: ALWAYS validate user input:
91: 
92: ```typescript
93: import { z } from 'zod'
94: 
95: const schema = z.object({
96:   email: z.string().email(),
97:   age: z.number().int().min(0).max(150)
98: })
99: 
100: const validated = schema.parse(input)
101: ```
102: 
103: ### Code Quality Checklist
104: 
105: Before marking work complete:
106: - [ ] Code is readable and well-named
107: - [ ] Functions are small (<50 lines)
108: - [ ] Files are focused (<800 lines)
109: - [ ] No deep nesting (>4 levels)
110: - [ ] Proper error handling

112: - [ ] No hardcoded values

259:

274: 
275: ```typescript
276: export function useDebounce<T>(value: T, delay: number): T {
277:   const [debouncedValue, setDebouncedValue] = useState<T>(value)
278: 
279:   useEffect(() => {
280:     const handler = setTimeout(() => setDebouncedValue(value), delay)
281:     return () => clearTimeout(handler)
282:   }, [value, delay])
283: 
284:   return debouncedValue
285: }

11: 
12: # Gran-Mestre — Meta-Orquestrador do OpenCode
13: 
14: ## Identidade
15: 
16: Você é o **Gran-Mestre**, o orquestrador central do OpenCode. Você é o **ponto de entrada único** para todas as requisições do usuário. Você **nunca executa trabalho bruto** — analisa, classifica e delega.
17: 
18: > "Não faço o trabalho. Faço o trabalho ser feito."
19: 
20: ## Como Usar
21: 
22: ```
23: /gran-mestre <descrição da tarefa>
24: ```
25: 
26: Flags opcionais:
27: - `--plan-only` — Só planejar, não executar
28: - `--execute-only` — Só executar plano existente
29: - `--review-only` — Só revisar código
30: 
31: ## Pipeline
32: 
33: ### 1. Classificar Complexidade
34: 
35: | Complexidade | Critério | Ação |
36: |---|---|---|
37: | **TRIVIAL** | 1 passo, sem side effects | Executa direto. Sem delegação. |
38: | **SIMPLE** | 2-3 passos, escopo fechado | Mini-plano em CONTEXT.md (3-5 linhas). Delega ao Atlas. |
39: | **MEDIUM** | 3-7 passos, múltiplos arquivos | Prometheus (plano) → Héstia (validação) → Atlas (execução) |
40: | **COMPLEX** | 7+ passos, arquitetura envolvida | Prometheus → Héstia → Superpowers → Atlas → Hephaestus/Atena (revisão) |
41: | **CRITICAL** | Produção, segurança, dados | Mesmo que COMPLEX + escalona para nuvem se falhar 2x |
42: | **FEATURE** | Design em aberto, requisito ambíguo | **Pipeline em Cascata** (Gran-Mestre + Superpowers em zíper) |
43: 
44: ### 2. Pipeline Padrão (MEDIUM+)
45: 
46: ```
47: Usuário → Gran-Mestre → Prometheus (planejar)
48:                        → Héstia (validar plano, max 3 ciclos)
49:                        → Atlas (executar, max 2 ciclos)
50:                        → Atena/Hephaestus (revisar, COMPLEX/CRITICAL only)
51:                        → Relatório ao usuário
52: ```
53: 
54: #### Agentes
55: 
56: | Agente | Função | Modelo |
57: |---|---|---|
58: | **Prometheus** | Decompor requisitos → PLAN.md | Qwen3.5 27B |
59: | **Héstia** | Validar plano antes/depois | Qwen3.5 27B |
60: | **Atlas** | Implementar o plano (ondas paralelas) | Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B |
61: | **Atena / Hephaestus** | Code review + qualidade | Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B |
62: | **Sisyphus** | Tarefas TRIVIAIS | Modelo fast |
63: 
64: #### Pipeline em Cascata (Rota FEATURE)
65: 
66: Intercalação em zíper entre Gran-Mestre e Superpowers:
67: 
68: ```
69: FASE 1 — Descoberta (27B): Prometheus → Brainstorming → GATE 1
70: FASE 2 — Contrato  (27B): Spec Writer → Héstia → GATE 2
71: FASE 3 — Plano     (27B): Plan Writer → Héstia → GATE 3 → 💾 SHA
72: FASE 4 — Execução  (30B): Atlas (supervisor) + Implementer (TDD) + Code Reviewer
73: FASE 5 — Revisão   (30B): Atena (diff total)
74: FASE 6 — Entrega   (27B): Verification → Héstia → GATE 4 → Memória
75: ```
76: 
77: Modos de gate:
78: - **`A` interativo** (default): 4 gates, máximo alinhamento
79: - **`C` autônomo**: Héstia como proxy (só escala ao usuário se reprovar 2x)
80: 
81: ### 3. Safety Protocol
82: 
83: ```
84: 1. ANTES de executar: git rev-parse HEAD → salvar SHA em CONTEXT.md
85: 2. Se falhar: git reset --hard {SHA}
86: 3. Máximo 1 rollback por pipeline
87: 4. Reportar ao usuário com 3 opções:
88:    - Tentar abordagem diferente
89:    - Revisar plano com Prometheus
90:    - Cancelar pipeline
91: 5. Aguardar decisão do usuário — NUNCA continuar rollback automático
92: ```
93: 
94: ### 4. Attestation (SHA-256 do Plano)
95: 
96: O Gran-Mestre **atesta a integridade** dos seus planos via SHA-256:
97: 
98: - Ao criar PLAN.md, calcula SHA-256 e armazena em `.plan-attestation`
99: - Antes de executar, verifica se o hash atual corresponde
100: - Se o plano foi adulterado → **bloqueia execução** e reporta
101: 
102: ```
103: Implementation:
104:   attest_plan <plan_file> → escreve SHA-256 em .plan-attestation
105:   verify_plan <plan_file> → compara SHA-256 atual com .plan-attestation
106: ```
107: 
108: ### 5. Completion Gate
109: 
110: O Gran-Mestre implementa **completion gate** no Stop hook:
111: 
112: - Ao final de cada resposta, verifica se a fase atual do plano está completa
113: - Se fase `in_progress` mas sem progresso detectado → notifica
114: - Em modo `--gated`, bloqueia o stop até o plano estar completo
115: 
116: ### 6. Observabilidade
117: 
118: Registrar após cada fase em CONTEXT.md:
119: ```
120: [Metrics] Phase: {decompose|plan|validate|execute|review}
121: [Metrics] Route: {TRIVIAL|SIMPLE|MEDIUM|COMPLEX|CRITICAL|FEATURE}
122: [Metrics] Status: {success|escalated|failed}
123: ```
124: 
125: Integração com OTel Collector + Jaeger (spans emitidos via `otel-span-emitter.py`).
126: 
127: ### 7. Shared Brain (Cerebral Memory)
128: 
129: Após pipeline completo:
130: 1. `cerebral_memory.ingest_source()` — contexto do pipeline
131: 2. `cerebral_memory.create_summary()` — aprendizados
132: 3. `cerebral_memory.upsert_entity()` — decisões chave
133: 4. `cerebral_memory.upsert_concept()` — padrões descobertos
134: 
135: ### 8. Template de PLAN.md
136: 
137: ```
138: # Plan: [Nome da Fase]
139: 
140: ## Goal
141: [Uma frase clara descrevendo o objetivo]
142: 
143: ## Tasks
144: ### Task 1: [Nome] ([wave])
145: - [ ] Descrição
146: - **Acceptance Criteria:** [critério]
147: - **Dependencies:** [nome das tasks]
148: 
149: ## Errors
150: | Error | Attempt | Resolution |
151: |---|---|---|
152: ```
153: 
154: ## Pre Tool Use — Validação de Plano
155: 
156: Antes de delegar ao Atlas, verificar:
157: 1. PLAN.md existe? Se não → criar via Prometheus primeiro
158: 2. PLAN.md tem ≥1 fase com acceptance criteria?
159: 3. PLAN.md tem ≥1 task por fase?
160: 4. Dependências listadas (se houver)?
161: 5. Attestation SHA-256 confere?
162: 6. Se plano incompleto → voltar ao Prometheus
163: 
164: ## Anti-Patterns
165: 
166: | Não Faça | Faça Instead |
167: |---|---|
168: | Executar código diretamente | Delegar para Atlas |
169: | Editar arquivos de implementação | Delegar para Atlas |
170: | Fazer research profundo sozinho | Delegar para explore/librarian |
171: | Tomar decisões sem validação | Passar pela Héstia |
172: | Continuar após rollback sem aprovação | Aguardar decisão do usuário |
173: | Pular gates no modo interativo | Respeitar os 4 gates |
174: | Repetir mesma ação após falha | Mutar abordagem (3-Strike Protocol) |
175: 
176: ## 3-Strike Error Protocol
177: 
178: ```
179: ATTEMPT 1: Diagnosticar e corrigir
180:   → Ler erro com atenção
181:   → Identificar causa raiz
182:   → Aplicar correção direcionada
183: 
184: ATTEMPT 2: Abordagem alternativa
185:   → Mesmo erro? Método diferente
186:   → Ferramenta diferente? Biblioteca diferente?
187:   → NUNCA repetir exatamente a mesma ação
188: 
189: ATTEMPT 3: Repensar abordagem
190:   → Questionar premissas
191:   → Pesquisar soluções
192:   → Considerar atualizar o plano
193: 
194: APÓS 3 FALHAS: Escalar ao usuário
195:   → Explicar o que foi tentado
196:   → Compartilhar o erro específico
197:   → Pedir orientação
198: ```
199: 
200: ## 2-Action Rule
201: 
202: > "After every 2 view/browser/search operations, IMMEDIATELY save key findings to text files."
203: 
204: Isso evita que informação visual/multimodal seja perdida quando o contexto é resetado.
205: 
206: ## Relatório Final
207: 
208: Sempre entregar ao usuário:
209: 1. **O que foi feito** — sumário executivo
210: 2. **Arquivos modificados** — lista completa
211: 3. **Testes** — passando/falhando
212: 4. **Avisos** — apenas avisos reais, não itens adiados
213: 5. **Recomendações** — follow-up sugerido
214:

217: | Caminho | Conteúdo |
218: |---|---|
219: | `~/.opencode/agent/gran-mestre.md` | Definição do agente (mode: primary) |

21: ## Setup
22: 
23: No dependency installation is required. The distributed skill includes standalone validators compiled from all five JSON Schemas, so schema and layout validation work immediately after installation. The generated HTML and the renderer runtime are both dependency-free.
24: 
25: Run `node bin/archify.mjs doctor` to verify an installation. Run `node bin/archify.mjs demo [output-directory]` to generate a ready-to-open example before creating the first custom diagram.
26: 
27: If you have no shell access at all (e.g. the skill was added as project knowledge), fall back to architecture mode for every request: hand-place SVG into `assets/template.html` following the Design System below, and run the self-review checklist before delivering.

29: ## Choosing a Diagram Type
30: 
31: When the request is ambiguous, run `node bin/archify.mjs guide "<the user's scenario>"` before choosing a renderer. The bundled zero-dependency guide selects one of 11 bounded scenario recipes and returns the question answered, when to use or avoid it, required evidence, presentation settings, and a copy-ready prompt. `--json` provides the same contract for automation, and `--lang en|zh` overrides language detection. Use the recommendation as a starting point, then verify it against the user's actual question and repository evidence.
32: 
33: Every bundled scenario recipe is backed by a checked-in, validated example in `examples/` and a generated Proof Lab card. Use those examples as structural references rather than copying their domain facts. When changing a recipe or proof example in the repository, regenerate both `docs/guide.html` and `docs/gallery.html`; tests enforce that all 11 recipe proof IDs resolve and that each proof retains three named reader views.

36: |------|---------|-----|
37: | `architecture` | System components, cloud resources, services, security boundaries, infrastructure | `renderers/architecture/render-architecture.mjs` + JSON (or hand-place SVG when renderers can't run) |

57: ## Layout principles (read before placing)
58: 
59: Archify's readability comes from **spatial narrative**, not from drawing every dependency as an arrow. Before you write coordinates or edge lists, plan one clear story:
60: 
61: 1. **One main path** — left → right (architecture) or lane → column (workflow). The reader should trace the happy path without crossing lines.
62: 2. **Few labeled edges** — label only cross-boundary or non-obvious transitions on the main path. Adjacent steps stay unlabeled.
63: 3. **Short side branches** — permissions, storage, bots, CI: connect **up or down** from the nearest node on the main path. Never route a secondary edge diagonally across unrelated components.
64: 4. **Cards for detail** — policies, tech stack notes, and "also connects to X" belong in summary cards, not as extra arrows.
65: 5. **Mode fit** — process / approval / tool-call stories → `workflow` or `sequence`. Component maps with ≤12 nodes → `architecture`. If the diagram needs 20+ edges, remove edges until the main path is obvious.
66: 
67: Worked examples on this pattern: `examples/archify-repo.architecture.json` (this repo) and `examples/maka-architecture.architecture.json` (third-party desktop app).
68: 
69: When validation fails on label overlap, read the **Suggested fix** lines (coordinates / `labelAt` / `labelDy`) and apply them directly — do not guess offsets blindly.

71: ## Renderer Modes (architecture / workflow / sequence / dataflow / lifecycle)
72: 
73: All five modes follow the same loop:
74: 
75: 1. **Read first**: the schema (`schemas/<type>.schema.json`) and the complete worked example (`examples/*.{architecture,workflow,sequence,dataflow,lifecycle}.json`) — copy its patterns instead of guessing field shapes.
76: 2. Write `<name>.<type>.json`.
77: 3. Render: `node bin/archify.mjs render <type> <input>.json <output>.html` (paths relative to this skill's folder).
78: 4. Validate the generated artifact: `node bin/archify.mjs validate <type> <input>.json --json`, explicitly add `--quality standard` for dense engineering diagrams or `--quality showcase` for polished delivery, or check an existing HTML file with `node bin/archify.mjs check <output>.html`. This catches malformed SVG output, non-finite SVG values, two-point diagonal arrows, arrows crossing the legend, and profile-aware relationship crossings.
79: 5. If either step fails, the error names the JSON path or the fix (thresholds, valid ranges, which knob to change). Fix the JSON and re-run; never edit the renderer.
80: 
81: Schema violations exit non-zero with path-prefixed messages like `/nodes/3 (id/label: "router") must NOT have additional properties`. The renderers additionally fail fast on established layout problems: node/state overlap (including cross-lane), labels colliding with nodes or other labels, labels wider than their node, out-of-range columns/rows, too-short edges, and legends outside the viewBox. New composition gates are deliberately opt-in for v1 stability: if neither `meta.quality_profile` nor CLI `--quality` is present, an older schema-v1 document stays renderable and detectable composition findings do not become new hard failures. For new or edited work, choose `standard` or `showcase` explicitly. Both profiles enforce unrelated-node Clean Flow and structural container-border rules; the shared Clean Flow Gate reports `clean-flow/edge-through-node`, the exact collection/index and optional relationship ID, obstacle ID, first intersecting segment, 2px clearance, and supported routing/placement knobs before output is written. The composition receipt separately reports final visible paths: unrelated proper X crossings warn in `standard` and fail in `showcase`; showcase also fails any sub-8px route segment and sub-16px interior turn while preserving ordinary 8–15px endpoint stubs. Shared semantic endpoints, endpoint touches, and collinear relationship corridors are not proper crossings. Source/target boxes are endpoints; boundaries, lanes, stages, lifecycle bands, sequence segments/lifelines/activations, and other containers remain intentional pass-through geometry. CJK text is measured at double width automatically.

83: Set `meta.animation: "trace"` only when the user asks for motion or a presentation/demo view. It adds lightweight SVG/CSS trace animation to renderer-marked arrows and nodes plus one explicit 44px `Live` / `Still` Motion Governor. Story, Chapter, Route, Lens, Relationship Preview, Intent Trace, Focus, and Legend remain stronger semantic owners. `Still` must reset every effect to complete static meaning, pause active Story playback at its exact beat, persist the reader choice when storage is available, and never auto-resume playback. Dynamic `prefers-reduced-motion` and page hiding use the same stop path. Static artifacts must never start decorative motion or show the control; embed remains calm unless `?play=1` explicitly requests one bounded chapter. Route Probe uses one finite signal and then leaves the exact route static. Canonical SVG and raster exports remain still; only the isolated WebM clone may explicitly opt into the repeatable finite trace timeline. Motion ownership is viewer-only, tokenized for stale-safe cleanup, and never enters schema, IR, renderer layout, or authored geometry.

Permit at most two selected kinds. One selected kind keeps its nodes and all touching relationships strong while connected peer endpoints remain contextual; two selected kinds keep only their direct authored cross-kind relationships strong and report both directions separately. After an explicit selection, Semantic Flow clones only the exact matched path/line/polyline geometry into a marker-free, pointer-free, `aria-hidden` runtime overlay: one-kind traffic distinguishes outgoing, incoming, and within-kind direction, while two-kind traffic distinguishes authored forward and reverse flow. Keep nodes, labels, camera, and original edges fixed; preserve preset identity, make reduced motion static, suppress flow above 24 matched edges, and omit the overlay in embed, print, and canonical export. Unrelated content must recede softly without being hidden, moved, rerouted, or removed from fitting. Closing the panel preserves the pinned state, `#lens=<kind>~<kind>` restores it, and Escape closes the panel before clearing the lens. Focus, Route Probe, and Story Trail clear Lens before taking ownership; active Lens suppresses Intent Trace. Matching renderer-owned Reading Depth detail remains visible. 133: 
134: Before a node is committed to focus, the shared viewer provides Intent Trace. Fine-pointer hover and keyboard focus must derive exactly the node's one-hop incoming, outgoing, and self-loop relationships from stable `data-edge-from`, `data-edge-to`, and `data-edge-key` hooks. Unrelated topology may recede, but authored edges, markers, dash patterns, labels, and geometry remain unchanged. The directional signal is a runtime-only clone of path/line/polyline geometry with markers and semantic attributes removed and `pathLength="1"` for a consistent rhythm. Touch skips the preview and retains one-tap focus. Active embed/story/focus/relationship-preview/pan state suppresses it, `prefers-reduced-motion` replaces movement with a static highlight, keyboard focus announces exact connection counts, and click/Enter/Space clears the temporary state before Semantic Passport takes ownership. Never add Intent Trace fields to JSON IR or include its overlay in canonical exports.

If one node is already focused it becomes the source; otherwise choose a source directly on the semantic SVG or through contextual Finder, then choose a highlighted reachable destination on-canvas or from the same search surface. Finder must omit dead-end sources, filter destinations by authored reachability, preview their shortest directed hop count, and keep the in-progress route when Finder closes. Traverse only `data-edge-from` → `data-edge-to`, ignore self-loops for two-endpoint routing, and use deterministic unweighted BFS in authored DOM edge order. The result must be the fewest real directed hops, keep exact ordered node and edge identity, frame only that route with Semantic Camera, and expose a compact node/hop receipt plus `#route=<source>~<target>` copy link. Never invent edge weights, fall back to an undirected path, mutate layout, or add route fields to JSON IR. Render every receipt stop as a native button with one roving Tab stop and add Previous, Next, Journey/Pause/Replay, and Overview controls. The full route stays visible. Position zero owns the source and no incoming edge; position `i > 0` owns exactly `activeEdges[i - 1]`, which alone may emit one finite 780ms marker-free signal. Manual activation pauses playback, while arrows/Home/End move focus and Enter/Space selects. Use Semantic Camera to frame previous/current/next; manual inspection remains available without motion. Escape layers as pause → Overview → clear. Keep `#route=<source>~<target>` endpoint-only and restore to Overview without autoplay. Every preset supports both themes. WebM export appears only for trace-enabled diagrams and records six seconds directly in a supporting browser.
141: 
142: ### Workflow
143: 
144: ```json
145: {
146:   "schema_version": 1,
147:   "diagram_type": "workflow",
148:   "meta": { "title": "Release Workflow", "subtitle": "PR to production", "output": "release.html" },
149:   "lanes": [ { "id": "dev", "label": "Developer" }, { "id": "ci", "label": "CI" }, { "id": "exceptions", "label": "Exception Handling", "variant": "exception" } ],
150:   "phases": [ { "id": "intake", "label": "Intake", "fromCol": 0, "toCol": 1 } ],
151:   "groups": [ { "id": "checks", "label": "Parallel checks", "lane": "ci", "fromCol": 1, "toCol": 3, "variant": "emphasis" } ],
152:   "mainPath": ["pr", "build"],
153:   "nodes": [
154:     { "id": "pr", "lane": "dev", "col": 0, "type": "frontend", "label": "Open PR", "sublabel": "feature branch" },
155:     { "id": "build", "lane": "ci", "col": 1, "type": "backend", "label": "Build", "sublabel": "lint + test", "tag": "blocking" }
156:   ],
157:   "edges": [
158:     { "id": "pr-to-build", "from": "pr", "to": "build", "label": "webhook", "variant": "emphasis", "fromSide": "bottom", "toSide": "top", "route": "drop" }
159:   ],
160:   "cards": []
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: **Layout budget**: 6 columns (`col` 0–5) at fixed x positions `[88, 220, 300, 430, 500, 625]` — columns 1↔2 and 3↔4 are only 70–80px apart, so default-width (92px) nodes in those adjacent columns of the same lane overlap; skip a column or shrink `width`. Lane content width is 640px. Omit `meta.viewBox` — the renderer sizes height to the lane count automatically. Use `phases` for top-of-diagram story beats, `groups` to frame parallel work or a branch inside one lane, and `lane.variant: "exception"` for error/retry/fallback lanes. `mainPath` is optional but recommended: list the happy-path node ids in order so the renderer can catch missing edges or accidental backward movement. Edge routes: `straight`, `drop` (bend between lanes; `bias` 0–1 picks where), `outside-right`, `return-left`, `bottom-channel`, `up-channel`, or explicit `via` points. Keep adjacent-step edges unlabeled; reserve labels for cross-lane transitions, approvals, async traces, and returns.
165: 
166: ### Sequence
167: 
168: ```json
169: {
170:   "schema_version": 1,
171:   "diagram_type": "sequence",
172:   "meta": { "title": "Cache Miss Request", "subtitle": "auth and cache fallback", "output": "cache-miss.html" },
173:   "participants": [
174:     { "id": "web", "type": "frontend", "label": "Web App", "sublabel": "React UI" },
175:     { "id": "api", "type": "backend", "label": "API", "sublabel": "handler" }
176:   ],
177:   "segments": [ { "from": 160, "to": 320, "label": "01 / AUTH" } ],
178:   "messages": [
179:     { "id": "request-data", "from": "web", "to": "api", "y": 200, "label": "GET /data", "variant": "emphasis" },
180:     { "id": "return-data", "from": "api", "to": "web", "y": 290, "label": "200 JSON", "variant": "return" }
181:   ],
182:   "activations": [ { "participant": "api", "from": 190, "to": 300, "type": "backend" } ],
183:   "cards": []
184: }
185: ```
186: 
187: **Layout budget**: participants sit at x = 62 + index×108, so a 920-wide viewBox fits at most 8. Message `y` must stay within `[160, viewBox_height − 83]`; messages that share horizontal space need ≥28px vertical separation; arrows need ≥60px horizontal span. `segments[].from/to` and `activations[].from/to` are **y pixel coordinates**, not participant ids. A taller `meta.viewBox` (default `[920, 760]`) buys more timeline room. Keep labels short: "GET /path", "verify JWT", "cache miss", "200 JSON".
188: 
189: ### Dataflow
190: 
191: ```json
192: {
193:   "schema_version": 1,
194:   "diagram_type": "dataflow",
195:   "meta": { "title": "Product Analytics", "subtitle": "events to consumers", "output": "analytics.html" },
196:   "stages": [ { "label": "Sources" }, { "label": "Ingest" }, { "label": "Store" } ],
197:   "nodes": [
198:     { "id": "web", "type": "frontend", "label": "Web App", "stage": 0, "row": 0, "sublabel": "clickstream" },
199:     { "id": "kafka", "type": "messagebus", "label": "Kafka", "stage": 1, "row": 0, "tag": "accepted events" }
200:   ],
201:   "flows": [
202:     { "id": "web-events", "from": "web", "to": "kafka", "label": "events", "classification": "PII touch", "variant": "emphasis" }
203:   ],
204:   "cards": []
205: }
206: ```
207: 
208: **Layout budget**: 2–5 stages at x = 100 + stage×215; 5 rows (`row` 0–4) at y `[128, 242, 356, 470, 584]`; default node 112×58. Default viewBox `[940, 720]`. Flow labels are mandatory and asset-like ("clickstream", "identity map", "feature vectors"); put sensitivity in `classification` ("PII touch", "approved only", "non-PII"). Variants: `emphasis` = primary path, `security` = PII/policy/consent, `dashed` = async/batch.
209: 
210: ### Lifecycle
211: 
212: ```json
213: {
214:   "schema_version": 1,
215:   "diagram_type": "lifecycle",
216:   "meta": { "title": "Agent Run Lifecycle", "subtitle": "states and terminal outcomes", "output": "agent-run.html" },
217:   "lanes": [
218:     { "id": "main", "label": "Lifecycle phases" },
219:     { "id": "waiting", "label": "Interruptions" },
220:     { "id": "terminal", "label": "Terminal exits" }
221:   ],
222:   "states": [
223:     { "id": "queued", "type": "start", "label": "Queued", "lane": "main", "col": 0, "step": "01" },
224:     { "id": "running", "type": "active", "label": "Executing", "lane": "main", "col": 2, "step": "02" },
225:     { "id": "approval", "type": "waiting", "label": "Needs Approval", "lane": "waiting", "col": 0 },
226:     { "id": "done", "type": "success", "label": "Completed", "lane": "terminal", "col": 2 }
227:   ],
228:   "transitions": [
229:     { "id": "start-running", "from": "queued", "to": "running", "variant": "emphasis" },
230:     { "id": "approval-needed", "from": "running", "to": "approval", "label": "needs approval", "variant": "security", "fromSide": "bottom", "toSide": "right" },
231:     { "id": "run-succeeded", "from": "running", "to": "done", "label": "success", "variant": "emphasis", "fromSide": "bottom", "toSide": "top" }
232:   ],
233:   "cards": []
234: }
235: ```
236: 
237: **Layout budget — lane ids are semantic and reserved**: `main` is required and maps to the top phase band (cols 0–4); `terminal` maps to the bottom outcome band (cols 0–2); **every other lane id shares the single middle event band** (cols 0–2) — separate same-band states with different `col` or `yOffset`. Band headers render from your lane labels. Default viewBox `[980, 660]`. Keep transition labels event-like and sparse ("retry", "timeout", "cancel"); prefer state `tag`s, `step` numbers, and summary cards over label-heavy arrows. Put terminal states in the `terminal` lane so endings are unambiguous.
238: 
239: ### Per-mode deep guidance
240: 
241: Each renderer has a README with its full design language (route presets, semantic types, story guidance): `renderers/workflow/README.md`, `renderers/sequence/README.md`, `renderers/dataflow/README.md`, `renderers/lifecycle/README.md`. Read the matching one before your first diagram of that mode in a session.
242: 
243: ## Architecture Mode
244: 
245: Architecture has the same read-schema-then-render loop as the other modes — prefer it. Hand-placed SVG is the fallback for when renderers can't run.
246: 
247: ```json
248: {
249:   "schema_version": 1,
250:   "diagram_type": "architecture",
251:   "meta": { "title": "Sample Web App", "subtitle": "3-tier SaaS on AWS", "output": "web-app.html" },
252:   "components": [
253:     { "id": "users", "type": "external", "label": "Users", "sublabel": "Browser", "pos": [40, 300] },
254:     { "id": "api", "type": "backend", "label": "API Server", "sublabel": "FastAPI :8000", "pos": [460, 300] },
255:     { "id": "db", "type": "database", "label": "PostgreSQL", "sublabel": ":5432", "pos": [680, 300] }
256:   ],
257:   "boundaries": [
258:     { "kind": "region", "label": "AWS us-west-2", "wraps": ["api", "db"] }
259:   ],
260:   "connections": [
261:     { "id": "users-to-api", "from": "users", "to": "api", "label": "HTTPS", "variant": "emphasis" },
262:     { "id": "api-to-db", "from": "api", "to": "db", "label": "SQL" }
263:   ],
264:   "cards": []
265: }
266: ```
267: 
268: Render: `node bin/archify.mjs render architecture <input>.json <output>.html`.
269: 
270: **Free placement** — `pos: [x, y]` is the component's top-left; `size: [w, h]` defaults to `[120, 60]`. Unlike typed modes there is no lane/stage grid — asymmetric placement is yours to choose. `meta.viewBox` is optional (auto-fitted).
271: 
272: **Grid placement (#8)** — when manual coordinates are painful, set semantic cells instead of doing arithmetic:
273: 
274: ```json
275: {
276:   "layout": { "mode": "grid", "cols": 7, "origin": [40, 100], "gapX": 24, "gapY": 48, "cellW": 120, "cellH": 60 },
277:   "components": [
278:     { "id": "agents", "type": "frontend", "label": "Agent Hosts", "row": 1, "col": 1 },
279:     { "id": "ir", "type": "messagebus", "label": "JSON IR", "row": 1, "col": 2 }
280:   ]
281: }
282: ```
283: 
284: `pos` still wins when present (override one cell). This is **not** auto-layout — spacing is fixed cell math. Example: `examples/archify-repo-grid.architecture.json`.
285: 
286: **Inspect layout (#9)** — after editing JSON, dump computed boxes without opening HTML:
287: 
288: ```bash
289: node bin/archify.mjs inspect architecture my.architecture.json
290: # or: node bin/archify.mjs validate architecture my.architecture.json --layout-json
291: ```
292: 
293: Output includes component rects, boundaries, connection point paths, and label positions.
294: 
295: **The renderer does the mechanical work that used to be hand-tuned**, so you only choose coordinates and meaning:
296: 
297: - **Free coordinates** — `pos: [x, y]` is the component's top-left; `size: [w, h]` defaults to `[120, 60]`. Unlike the typed modes there is no lane/stage grid — asymmetric placement is yours to choose. `meta.viewBox` is optional (auto-fitted to your components + a legend row).
298: - **Grid placement** — optional `layout.mode: "grid"` with `row`/`col` per component (see above). Not dagre; fixed cell spacing only.
299: - **Boundaries from `wraps`** — list the component ids a `region` (dashed amber) or `security-group` (dashed rose) encloses; the renderer computes the box with correct 30/50 padding automatically. Never hand-arithmetic a boundary again.
300: - **Connections** route like edges (`variant`, `fromSide`/`toSide`, `route: straight|orthogonal-h|orthogonal-v|auto`, `via`, `labelDx/labelDy/labelAt`). For a vertical labeled connection, push the label into the gap with `labelDy` (the validator will tell you if it lands on a box).

1: # Task Plan: Autofagia do Gran-Mestre
2: 
3: ## Goal
4: Aplicar a metodologia `planning-with-files` (OthmanAdi, v3.7.0) ao próprio Gran-Mestre — identificar gaps, implementar melhorias e fechar o ciclo de autofagia (dogfooding).
5: 
6: ## Current Phase
7: Phase 4 — Documentar Protocolos
8: 
9: ## Phases
10: 
11: ### Phase 1: Pesquisa e Análise Comparativa ✅
12: - [x] Fetch README, SKILL.md, templates, quickstart do planning-with-files
13: - [x] Fetch template task_plan.md, findings.md, progress.md
14: - [x] Extrair lista de inovações vs GSD atual
15: - [x] Documentar gaps no findings.md
16: - **Status:** complete
17: 
18: ### Phase 2: Criar Estrutura de Autofagia ✅
19: - [x] Criar .planning/autofagia/ com task_plan.md, findings.md, progress.md
20: - [x] Documentar comparação GSD vs PWF
21: - [x] Instalar skill planning-with-files oficialmente (se compatível)
22: - [x] Mapear quais inovações implementar vs quais ignorar
23: - **Status:** complete
24: 
25: ### Phase 3: Implementar Gaps Prioritários ✅
26: - [x] **Criar SKILL.md do Gran-Mestre** (gap crítico — arquivo ausente)
27: - [x] **Implementar Attestation** (SHA-256 nos PLAN.md + verificação em hooks)
28: - [x] **Implementar Completion Gate** (verificar plano completo no Stop hook)
29: - [x] **Criar findings.md dedicado** para cada fase
30: - [x] **Implementar Ledger** (JSONL append-only para rastreamento)
31: - **Status:** complete
32: 
33: ### Phase 4: Documentar Protocolos ✅
34: - [x] Atualizar agent/gran-mestre.md com novos protocolos
35: - [x] Adicionar 2-Action Rule e 3-Strike Protocol
36: - [x] Atualizar SKILL.md com referências a attestation/completion gate
37: - [x] Criar docs/autofagia.md com documentação completa
38: - **Status:** complete
39: 
40: ### Phase 5: Testar Ciclo Completo
41: - [ ] Rodar `/gran-mestre` com uma tarefa real usando a nova estrutura
42: - [ ] Verificar completion gate funcionando
43: - [ ] Verificar attestation
44: - [ ] Verificar findings.md sendo populado
45: - **Status:** pending
46: 
47: ### Phase 6: Reportar Resultados ✅
48: - [x] Relatório final da autofagia
49: - [ ] Recomendações de follow-up
50: - **Status:** complete
51: 
52: ## Key Questions
53: 1. Quais inovações do planning-with-files são aplicáveis ao Gran-Mestre?
54: 2. Quais já existem no GSD mas com nomes diferentes?
55: 3. O completion gate é compatível com o modelo de hooks do OpenCode?
56: 4. Vale a pena instalar o planning-with-files como skill separada ou incorporar as ideias?
57: 
58: ## Decisions Made
59: | Decision | Rationale |
60: |----------|-----------|
61: | Usar diretório .planning/ autofagia/ | Isolado do .planning/ GSD existente, segue padrão PWF de planos escoped |

1: # Protocolos do Gran-Mestre
2: 
3: Versão 6.1 — Atualizado com Autofagia (planning-with-files + AAS)
4: 
5: ## 1. Roteamento por Complexidade
6: 
7: | Complexidade | Critério | Pipeline | Agentes |
8: |---|---|---|---|
9: | **TRIVIAL** | 1 passo, sem side effects | Execução direta | Sisyphus |
10: | **SIMPLE** | 2-3 passos, escopo fechado | Mini-plano → Atlas | Atlas |
11: | **MEDIUM** | 3-7 passos, múltiplos arquivos | Prometheus → Héstia → Atlas | 3 agentes |
12: | **COMPLEX** | 7+ passos, arquitetura envolvida | Prometheus → Héstia → Superpowers → Atlas → Atena | 5 agentes |
13: | **CRITICAL** | Produção, segurança, dados | Mesmo que COMPLEX + escalona se falhar 2x | 5 agentes |
14: | **FEATURE** | Design em aberto, requisito ambíguo | Pipeline em Cascata | 6+ agentes |
15: 
16: ## 2. Safety Protocol
17: 
18: ```
19: 1. ANTES de executar: git rev-parse HEAD → salvar SHA em CONTEXT.md
20: 2. Se falhar: git reset --hard {SHA}
21: 3. Máximo 1 rollback por pipeline
22: 4. Reportar ao usuário com 3 opções:
23:    - Tentar abordagem diferente
24:    - Revisar plano com Prometheus
25:    - Cancelar pipeline
26: 5. Aguardar decisão do usuário — NUNCA continuar rollback automático
27: ```
28: 
29: ## 3. Attestation (SHA-256 do Plano)
30: 
31: O Gran-Mestre **atesta a integridade** dos seus planos via SHA-256:
32: 
33: ```bash
34: # Store attestation
35: ./scripts/attest-plan.sh store PLAN.md
36: 
37: # Verify attestation
38: ./scripts/attest-plan.sh verify PLAN.md
39: 
40: # Check (return 0/1)
41: ./scripts/attest-plan.sh check PLAN.md
42: ```
43: 
44: **Hook PreToolUse:** Verifica attestation antes de delegar para Atlas.
45: 
46: ## 4. Completion Gate
47: 
48: O Gran-Mestre implementa **completion gate** no Stop hook:
49: 
50: ```bash
51: # Check if plan is complete
52: ./scripts/check-plan-complete.sh PLAN.md
53: ```
54: 
55: **Comportamento:**
56: - Se plano incompleto → notifica e sugere continuar
57: - Se plano completo → permite parada normal
58: - Em modo `--gated` → bloqueia até plano completo
59: 
60: ## 5. 2-Action Rule
61: 
62: > "After every 2 view/browser/search operations, IMMEDIATELY save key findings to text files."
63: 
64: Isso evita que informação visual/multimodal seja perdida quando o contexto é resetado.
65: 
66: **Aplicado em:**
67: - `findings.md` — descobertas de pesquisa
68: - `progress.md` — log de sessão
69: - `task_plan.md` — progresso do plano
70: 
71: ## 6. 3-Strike Error Protocol
72: 
73: ```
74: ATTEMPT 1: Diagnosticar e corrigir
75:   → Ler erro com atenção
76:   → Identificar causa raiz
77:   → Aplicar correção direcionada
78: 
79: ATTEMPT 2: Abordagem alternativa
80:   → Mesmo erro? Método diferente
81:   → Ferramenta diferente? Biblioteca diferente?
82:   → NUNCA repetir exatamente a mesma ação
83: 
84: ATTEMPT 3: Repensar abordagem
85:   → Questionar premissas
86:   → Pesquisar soluções
87:   → Considerar atualizar o plano
88: 
89: APÓS 3 FALHAS: Escalar ao usuário
90: ```
91: 
92: ## 7. Observabilidade
93: 
94: Registrar após cada fase em CONTEXT.md:
95: ```
96: [Metrics] Phase: {decompose|plan|validate|execute|review}
97: [Metrics] Route: {TRIVIAL|SIMPLE|MEDIUM|COMPLEX|CRITICAL|FEATURE}
98: [Metrics] Status: {success|escalated|failed}
99: ```
100: 
101: ## 8. Shared Brain (Cerebral Memory)
102: 
103: ```
104: 1. ingest_source() — contexto do pipeline
105: 2. create_summary() — aprendizados
106: 3. upsert_entity() — decisões chave
107: 4. upsert_concept() — padrões descobertos
108: ```
109: 
110: ## 9. Pipeline em Cascata (FEATURE)
111: 
112: ```
113: FASE 1 — Descoberta (27B): Prometheus → Brainstorming → GATE 1
114: FASE 2 — Contrato  (27B): Spec Writer → Héstia → GATE 2
115: FASE 3 — Plano     (27B): Plan Writer → Héstia → GATE 3 → 💾 SHA
116: FASE 4 — Execução  (30B): Atlas (supervisor) + Implementer (TDD) + Code Reviewer
117: FASE 5 — Revisão   (30B): Atena (diff total)
118: FASE 6 — Entrega   (27B): Verification → Héstia → GATE 4 → Memória
119: ```
120: 
121: ## 10. Integração com AAS (antigravity-awesome-skills)
122: 
123: **Conceitos transferíveis:**
124: - Agent-First Control Plane → MCP local para discovery de skills
125: - AAS Core Stack Validation → compose_stack do Gran-Mestre
126: - Specialized Plugins → bundles por domínio (Security, DevOps, QA)
127: 
128: **Recursos AAS:** 1,969+ skills catalog, 15.1.0

1: # Findings & Decisions — Autofagia do Gran-Mestre
2: 
3: ## Requirements
4: - Aplicar planning-with-files (PWF) ao Gran-Mestre
5: - Identificar gaps entre GSD e PWF
6: - Implementar melhorias prioritárias
7: - Fechar ciclo de autofagia
8: 
9: ## Research Findings
10: 
11: ### O que é planning-with-files (PWF)
12: - Repositório: https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files
13: - Versão: v3.7.0 (Jul 2026)
14: - Stars: 25.6k, Forks: 2.2k
15: - Benchmark: 96.7% pass rate
16: - Licença: MIT
17: - Autor: OthmanAdi
18: - Concorrente direto vendido por $2B (Manus → Meta)
19: 
20: ### Core Pattern
21: ```
22: Context Window = RAM (volatile, limited)
23: Filesystem = Disk (persistent, unlimited)
24: → Anything important gets written to disk.
25: ```
26: 
27: Três arquivos de planejamento:
28: 1. `task_plan.md` — Fases, progresso, decisões
29: 2. `findings.md` — Pesquisa, descobertas, decisões técnicas
30: 3. `progress.md` — Log de sessão, resultados de teste
31: 
32: ### Inovações vs GSD
33: 
34: #### 1. UserPromptSubmit Hook (PWF-only)
35: PWF injeta o plano **a cada prompt do usuário**, não apenas antes de ferramentas. O PreToolUse injeta um resumo menor. O GSD só injeta contexto via CONTEXT.md manualmente.
36: 
37: #### 2. Attestation (SHA-256)
38: PWF calcula SHA-256 do `task_plan.md` e armazena em `.plan-attestation` (root) ou `.attestation` (scoped). Antes de injetar, verifica se o hash atual corresponde. Se não → **PLAN TAMPERED — injection blocked**.
39: 
40: O GSD tem Safety SHA (salvo antes de executar), mas é para rollback, não para integridade do plano.
41: 
42: #### 3. Completion Gate
43: PWF tem um `check-complete.sh` que verifica se TODAS as fases estão completas. Se não estiverem, o Stop hook notifica. Em modo `--gated`, o Stop hook bloqueia ativamente.
44: 
45: O GSD não tem nada equivalente — o agente pode simplesmente parar no meio.
46: 
47: #### 4. Session Recovery
48: PWF tem `session-catchup.py` que verifica se há contexto não sincronizado de sessões anteriores (via timestamps de arquivos, git diff).
49: 
50: O GSD tem `gsd-resume-work` mas depende de session-data salvos.
51: 
52: #### 5. Plan Resolution (múltiplos escopos)
53: PWF resolve planos em ordem:
54: 1. `$PLAN_ID` (env var) → `.planning/$PLAN_ID/`
55: 2. `.planning/.active_plan` → arquivo com slug
56: 3. `.planning/*/` → diretório mais recente com `task_plan.md`
57: 4. Raiz → `task_plan.md` no diretório atual
58: 
59: O GSD usa `.planning/` direto com fase numerada.
60: 
61: #### 6. Ledger (JSONL)
62: PWF v3.0+ tem `ledger-append`, `ledger-summary`, `phase-status` — append-only JSONL run ledger.
63: 
64: O GSD usa CONTEXT.md com texto livre.
65: 
66: #### 7. 2-Action Rule
67: PWF: "After every 2 view/browser/search operations, IMMEDIATELY save key findings to text files."
68: 
69: GSD: Não tem regra equivalente.
70: 
71: #### 8. 3-Strike Error Protocol
72: PWF formaliza: Attempt 1 (diagnose) → Attempt 2 (alternative) → Attempt 3 (broader rethink) → Escalate.
73: 
74: GSD: Tem retry-classifier com 8 categorias de erro, mas não formaliza o protocolo de 3 tentativas.
75: 
76: #### 9. Templates
77: PWF tem templates ricos com comentários explicativos (WHAT, WHY, WHEN, EXAMPLE).
78: 
79: GSD: PLAN.md é mais enxuto, sem exemplos inline.
80: 
81: #### 10. Suporte a 60+ agents
82: PWF instala em 60+ IDEs (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Kiro, OpenCode, etc.) via SKILL.md standard.
83: 
84: GSD: Só funciona no ecossistema OpenCode.
85: 
86: ### Gap Analysis Summary
87: 
88: | Inovação PWF | GSD Atual | Gap | Prioridade |
89: |---|---|---|---|
90: | **SKILL.md** | Skills/gran-mestre/SKILL.md **AUSENTE** | 🔴 CRÍTICO | Alta |
91: | **Attestation (SHA-256)** | Safety SHA (só rollback) | 🟡 MÉDIO | Alta |
92: | **Completion Gate** | Não existe | 🟡 MÉDIO | Alta |
93: | **findings.md** | RESEARCH.md (parcial) | 🟢 BAIXO | Média |
94: | **Ledger (JSONL)** | CONTEXT.md (texto livre) | 🟢 BAIXO | Média |
95: | **Session Recovery** | gsd-resume-work (similar) | 🟢 BAIXO | Baixa |
96: | **Plan Resolution** | .planning/ (simples) | 🟢 BAIXO | Baixa |
97: | **2-Action Rule** | Não existe | 🟢 BAIXO | Baixa |
98: | **3-Strike Protocol** | RetryClassifier (parcial) | 🟢 BAIXO | Baixa |
99: | **UserPromptSubmit Hook** | Não existe | 🟡 MÉDIO | Média |
100: 
101: ### Decisão: Incorporar vs Instalar
102: 
103: **Opção A — Instalar PWF como skill:**
104: - ✅ Acesso imediato a toda infraestrutura PWF
105: - ❌ Hooks conflitantes com hooks existentes do Gran-Mestre
106: - ❌ Dois sistemas de planejamento concorrentes
107: 
108: **Opção B — Incorporar ideias seletivamente:**
109: - ✅ Sem conflito de hooks
110: - ✅ Evolução natural do GSD
111: - ❌ Mais trabalho manual
112: - ✅ SKILL.md precisa ser criado de qualquer forma (gap existente)
113: 
114: **Decisão: Opção B — Incorporar.**
115: 
116: ## Technical Decisions
117: | Decision | Rationale |
118: |----------|-----------|
119: | Incorporar ideias, não instalar PWF | Evita conflito de hooks; SKILL.md já é gap conhecido |
120: | Priorizar SKILL.md + Attestation + Completion Gate | 3 gaps mais críticos para integridade do pipeline |
121: | SKILL.md em skills/gran-mestre/ | Localização padrão do OpenCode para skills |
122: | Attestation via SHA-256 no PLAN.md | Mesmo mecanismo do Safety SHA, mas para integridade do plano |
123: | Completion Gate no Stop hook | Verifica se fase atual está completa antes de permitir parada |
124: | findings.md por fase | Em vez de RESEARCH.md global, um findings.md por diretório de fase |
125: | Ledger JSONL opcional | Pode ser adicionado depois como complemento ao CONTEXT.md |
126: 
127: ## Issues Encountered
128: | Issue | Resolution |
129: |-------|------------|
130: | Skills/gran-mestre/SKILL.md ausente | Criar como parte da autofagia |
131: | Hooks.json já tem 30+ hooks | Novo hook de attestation precisa ser não-blocking |
132: | Completion gate pode conflitar com stop:format-typecheck | Implementar como check não-blocking (modo advisório) |
133: 
134: ## Resources
135: - Repo PWF: https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files
136: - Repo AAS: https://github.com/sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills
137: - Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vg2ypKmtK8M
138: - SKILL.md standard: https://skill-management.github.io/skill-standard/
139: - OpenCode docs: ~/.opencode/docs/
140: - Gran-Mestre agent: ~/.opencode/agent/gran-mestre.md
141: - Gran-Mestre manifesto: ~/.config/opencode/registry/GRAN_MESTRE.md
142: 
143: ## Inovações do AAS (antigravity-awesome-skills)
144: 
145: O AAS (Agentic Awesome Skills) complementa o planning-with-files com:
146: 
147: | Inovação AAS | Descrição | Aplicável ao Gran-Mestre? |
148: |---|---|---|
149: | **Agent-First Control Plane** | MCP local para busca/validação de skills | ✅ Sim — para discovery de skills |
150: | **1,969+ Skills Catalog** | Catálogo completo de skills | ✅ Sim — como referência |
151: | **AAS Core v15.1.0** | Stack validation, immutable planning | ✅ Sim — conceito transferível |
152: | **Specialized Plugins** | Plugins por domínio (Security, DevOps, QA) | ✅ Sim — integrar ao Gran-Mestre |
153: | **Workbench** | Review browser-local de stacks | ❌ Não essencial |
154: | **Agent Selection** | Agente escolhe skills, não rankings | ✅ Sim — refletir em decisões |
155: 
156: ### Decisão sobre AAS
157: 
158: **Integrar conceitos do AAS ao Gran-Mestre:**
159: - Usar `AAS Core Stack Validation` como modelo para `compose_stack` do Gran-Mestre
160: - Criar `specialized-plugins.md` no docs/ do Gran-Mestre
161: - Adicionar `catalog_search` capability ao Gran-Mestre (via MCP local)
162: 
163: **Não instalar AAS como skill separada:**
164: - Conflito de arquitetura (AAS é control plane, Gran-Mestre é orchestrator)
165: - Melhor incorporar conceitos seletivamente
166: 
167: ## Visual/Browser Findings
168: - README do PWF mostra 60+ IDEs suportados
169: - Banner v3: "Manus-style persistent file-based planning"
170: - 317 commits, 25.6k stars (crescimento explosivo em <24h)
171: - Benchmark: 2.7x faster recovery vs 6 methods
172: - Community forks: devis, multi-manus-planning, plan-cascade
