1: # Protocolos — Autofagia Cross-Harness (ECC + Gran-Mestre)
2: 
3: ## Arquitetura de Integração
4: 
5: ```
6: Gran-Mestre (Orquestrador)
7:     │
8:     ├── ECC (Performance & Hooks)
9:     │   ├── 67 agents → delegar tarefas especializadas
10:     │   ├── 261 skills → workflows reutilizáveis
11:     │   ├── 30+ hooks → lifecycle automation
12:     │   └── rules/ → regras universais
13:     │
14:     ├── Claude-Mem (Memória Persistente)
15:     │   ├── SQLite + Chroma → armazenamento vetorial
16:     │   ├── MCP Search → busca semântica
17:     │   └── Compressão AI → resumo de sessões
18:     │
19:     └── Planning-with-Files (Planejamento)
20:         ├── Attestation → SHA-256
21:         ├── Completion Gate → verificação de fases
22:         └── Ledger → rastreamento JSONL
23: ```
24: 
25: ## Protocolo 1: Attestation Cross-Harness
26: 
27: ```bash
28: # ECC Plugin Hook (PreToolUse)
29: # Verifica integridade do plano antes de executar
30: ECC_ATTEST_ENABLED=true  # default: false
31: 
32: # Attestation check
33: ecc-attest.sh verify .planning/task_plan.md
34: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
35:   echo "[ECC-Attest] ❌ Plano adulterado — execução bloqueada"
36:   exit 1
37: fi
38: ```
39: 
40: **Configuração:**
41: - Adicionar ao `hooks.json` do ECC como PreToolUse hook
42: - Matcher: `tool == "Write" && file_path matches "\\.planning/"`
43: - Usar `ecc-attest.sh` para store/verify/check
44: 
45: ## Protocolo 2: Completion Gate
46: 
47: ```bash
48: # ECC Stop Hook
49: # Verifica se fase atual está completa
50: ECC_COMPLETION_GATE=true  # default: false
51: 
52: ecc-complete.sh check .planning/task_plan.md
53: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
54:   echo "[ECC-Gate] ⚠️  Fases pendentes detectadas"
55:   ecc-complete.sh list-pending .planning/task_plan.md
56: fi
57: ```
58: 
59: **Configuração:**
60: - Adicionar ao `hooks.json` do ECC como Stop hook
61: - Usar env var `ECC_COMPLETION_GATE` para controle
62: - Modo gated: `ECC_COMPLETION_GATE=strict` bloqueia parada
63: 
64: ## Protocolo 3: 2-Action Rule (ECC)
65: 
66: ```
67: A cada 2 operações de leitura/pesquisa:
68:   1. Salvar descobertas em .planning/findings.md
69:   2. Atualizar .planning/progress.md
70:   3. Verificar se há gaps identificados
71: ```
72: 
73: **Implementação no ECC:**
74: - Hook PostToolUse com contador
75: - Reseta a cada 2 matches de `tool == "Grep" || tool == "Read" || tool == "WebSearch"`
76: - Escreve em `.planning/autofagia-ecc/findings.md`
77: 
78: ## Protocolo 4: 3-Strike Error Protocol (ECC)
79: 
80: ```
81: ATTEMPT 1: Diagnosticar (hook PreToolUse registra tentativa)
82: ATTEMPT 2: Abordagem alternativa (hook PostToolUse registra resultado)
83: ATTEMPT 3: Repensar abordagem (hook Stop registra falha final)
84: ESCALAR: Notificar usuário + sugerir próximo passo
85: ```
86: 
87: **Implementação no ECC:**
88: - Usar `ECC_ERROR_COUNTER` como env var
89: - Registrar em `~/.ecc/autofagia/error-log.jsonl`
90: - Escalar via comando `/escalate` ou notificação
91: 
92: ## Protocolo 5: Safety SHA Rollback
93: 
94: ```bash
95: # Antes de qualquer execução que modifique arquivos
96: SHA_BEFORE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
97: echo "[ECC-Safety] SHA: $SHA_BEFORE" >> .planning/context.md
98: 
99: # Se falhar
100: git reset --hard $SHA_BEFORE
101: echo "[ECC-Safety] ✅ Rollback executado para $SHA_BEFORE"
102: ```
103: 
104: ## Protocolo 6: Continuous Learning Integration
105: 
106: ```
107: ECC Continuous Learning v2
108:     │
109:     ├── Observa → registra em observations.jsonl
110:     ├── Analisa → thresholds de confiança
111:     ├── Instinto → regra automática com score
112:     └── Promove → skill quando score > 0.8
113:         │
114:         ▼
115: Gran-Mestre Autofagia
116:     │
117:     ├── Lê instintos do ECC
118:     ├── Correlaciona com gaps identificados
119:     ├── Propor melhorias no task_plan.md
120:     └── Fecha ciclo de autofagia
121: ```
122: 
123: ## Protocolo 7: Cross-Harness Adapter
124: 
125: ```yaml
126: autofagia-adapter:
127:   claude-code:
128:     hooks: native plugin hooks
129:     skills: SKILL.md + commands/
130:     rules: rules/common/ + rules/typescript/
131:     
132:   opencode:
133:     hooks: plugin events (gran-mestre bridge)
134:     skills: skills/ + commands/
135:     rules: rules/common/ adaptadas
136:     
137:   codex:
138:     hooks: instruction-backed (no native hooks)
139:     skills: AGENTS.md + skills/
140:     rules: rules/common/ via instruction
141:     
142:   cursor:

1: # Findings & Decisions — Autofagia do ECC (affaan-m/ECC)
2: 
3: ## Requirements
4: - Aplicar autofagia ao repositório ECC (230K ⭐)
5: - Identificar gaps na arquitetura de hooks, agents e skills
6: - Propor melhorias baseadas em Gran-Mestre + planning-with-files + Claude-Mem
7: - Criar scripts de integração cross-harness
8: 
9: ## Research Findings
10: 
11: ### O que é ECC?
12: ECC (Everything Claude Code) é um **sistema de otimização de performance para harnesses de agentes AI**. Vencedor de hackathon da Anthropic, com 10+ meses de desenvolvimento intensivo.
13: 
14: **Estatísticas:**
15: - ⭐ 230.000+ estrelas no GitHub
16: - 🧠 67 agentes especializados (planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide, architect, etc.)
17: - 📋 261+ skills workflows
18: - 🔌 30+ lifecycle hooks
19: - 🌐 Suporte a 8+ harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, Copilot, OpenClaw)
20: - 📦 297 releases em 10 meses
21: - 👥 110 contribuidores
22: 
23: ### Arquitetura ECC
24: ```
25: ECC/
26: ├── .claude-plugin/       # Plugin e marketplace manifests
27: ├── agents/               # 67 subagentes especializados
28: ├── skills/               # 261+ workflows (primary surface)
29: ├── commands/             # Slash commands (/tdd, /plan, /e2e, etc.)
30: ├── hooks/                # Lifecycle hooks (30+)
31: │   ├── hooks.json        # Config principal
32: │   ├── memory-persistence/  # Hooks de sessão
33: │   ├── strategic-compact/   # Sugestões de compactação
34: │   └── README.md         # Documentação
35: ├── rules/                # Regras universais + linguagem-específicas
36: │   ├── common/           # Princípios universais (sempre instalar)
37: │   ├── typescript/       # TypeScript/JavaScript
38: │   ├── python/           # Python
39: │   ├── golang/           # Go
40: │   └── ...               # 10+ linguagens
41: ├── scripts/              # Utilitários Node.js
42: ├── tests/                # Suite de testes
43: ├── contexts/             # Injeção de contexto dinâmico
44: ├── mcp-configs/          # Configurações MCP
45: └── ecc_dashboard.py      # Dashboard Tkinter
46: ```
47: 
48: ### Inovações do ECC vs Gran-Mestre
49: 
50: #### 1. Continuous Learning v2 (ECC-only)
51: ECC tem um sistema de aprendizado contínuo baseado em **instintos**:
52: - Observa ferramentas usadas (PreToolUse + PostToolUse)
53: - Extrai padrões com thresholds de confiança
54: - Cria instintos (regras automáticas) com metadados de confiança
55: - Promove instintos para skills quando maduros
56: 
57: **Comparação:** Gran-Mestre não tem equivalente. Claude-Mem é memória, não aprendizado.
58: 
59: #### 2. Cross-Harness Architecture (ECC-only)
60: ECC é projetado para funcionar em **múltiplos harnesses** com adaptadores:
61: - Claude Code (plugin nativo)
62: - Codex (plugin metadata + AGENTS.md)
63: - Cursor (regras adaptadas)
64: - OpenCode (plugin/event system adapter)
65: - Gemini (superfície de compatibilidade)
66: 
67: **Comparação:** Gran-Mestre é específico OpenCode. ECC é multi-harness.
68: 
69: #### 3. Hook Runtime Controls (ECC-only)
70: ECC permite controle de hooks via **variáveis de ambiente**:
71: - `ECC_HOOK_PROFILE` — minimal/standard/strict
72: - `ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS` — desabilitar hooks específicos
73: - `ECC_GATEGUARD` — gate de segurança
74: - `ECC_SESSION_START_MAX_CHARS` — limite de contexto
75: 
76: **Comparação:** Gran-Mestre tem gates fixos, não configuráveis por env vars.
77: 
78: #### 4. Async Hooks (ECC-only)
79: ECC suporta hooks **assíncronos** que não bloqueiam a execução:
80: ```json
81: {
82:   "type": "command",
83:   "command": "node slow-hook.js",
84:   "async": true,
85:   "timeout": 30
86: }
87: ```
88: 
89: **Comparação:** Gran-Mestre não tem hooks assíncronos.
90: 
91: #### 5. Strategic Compaction (ECC-only)
92: ECC tem sugestões de compactação estratégica para reduzir tokens:
93: - Análise de observações acumuladas
94: - Sugestões de resumo
95: - Preparação para nova sessão
96: 
97: **Comparação:** Claude-Mem faz compactação semântica, ECC faz estratégica.
98: 
99: ### Inovações do Gran-Mestre não presentes no ECC
100: 
101: | Inovação Gran-Mestre | Descrição | Gap no ECC | Prioridade |
102: |---|---|---|---|
103: | **Attestation (SHA-256)** | Verificação de integridade de planos | 🔴 Não existe | Alta |
104: | **Completion Gate** | Verifica se plano está completo | 🟡 Parcial (ECC_GATEGUARD) | Alta |
105: | **2-Action Rule** | Salvar findings a cada 2 ações | 🔴 Não existe | Média |
106: | **3-Strike Protocol** | 3 tentativas antes de escalar | 🟡 Parcial (retry embutido) | Média |
107: | **SKILL.md padrão** | Metadados YAML + regras | 🟡 Migração em andamento | Média |
108: | **Safety SHA rollback** | SHA antes de executar | 🔴 Não existe | Alta |
109: | **Cerebral Memory** | Shared Brain pós-pipeline | 🟡 Parcial (continuous learning) | Média |
110: 
111: ### Inovações do planning-with-files não presentes no ECC
112: 
113: | Inovação PWF | Descrição | Gap no ECC |
114: |---|---|---|
115: | **planning-with-files** | Arquivos de plano persistentes | 🟡 Skills já fazem isso parcialmente |
116: | **Ledger JSONL** | Rastreamento append-only | 🔴 Não existe |
117: | **Session Recovery** | Recuperação de sessão via timestamps | 🟡 Parcial (memory-persistence) |
118: | **UserPromptSubmit Hook** | Injeção de plano a cada prompt | 🟡 Não explicita |
119: 
120: ### Inovações do Claude-Mem não presentes no ECC
121: 
122: | Inovação Claude-Mem | Descrição | Gap no ECC |
123: |---|---|---|
124: | **Memória persistente vetorial** | Chroma + SQLite FTS5 | 🟡 Usa JSONL + instintos |
125: | **MCP Search Tools** | search/timeline/get_observations | 🔴 Não existe |
126: | **Web Viewer UI** | Dashboard em tempo real | 🟡 Tem dashboard Tkinter |
127: | **Cloud Sync** | Backup para cmem.ai | 🔴 Não existe |
128: | **Compressão semântica AI** | Resumo automático de sessões | 🟡 Strategic compaction é manual |
129: 
130: ### Análise de Integração
131: 
132: ```
133:                     ┌─────────────────┐
134:                     │   Gran-Mestre   │
135:                     │  (Orquestrador) │
136:                     └────────┬────────┘
137:                              │
138:               ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
139:               │              │              │
140:               ▼              ▼              ▼
141:      ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
142:      │     ECC      │ │Claude-Mem│ │ Planning-w-F  │
143:      │ (Performance)│ │ (Memory) │ │  (Filesystem) │
144:      └──────────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────────┘
145: ```
146: 
147: **Os quatro sistemas são complementares:**
148: 1. **Gran-Mestre** — Orquestrador de alto nível, plano-delegação-revisão
149: 2. **ECC** — Otimização de harness, agents, skills, hooks, regras
150: 3. **Claude-Mem** — Memória persistente vetorial cross-sessão
151: 4. **Planning-with-Files** — Planejamento baseado em arquivos (SHA, gates)
152: 
153: ## Technical Decisions
154: | Decision | Rationale |
155: |----------|-----------|
156: | Criar scripts de autofagia ECC localmente | Não é possível fazer PR no repo remoto, mas scripts de análise são úteis |
157: | Foco em Attestation + Completion Gate | São os gaps mais críticos e já implementamos no Gran-Mestre |
158: | Integração cross-harness via adapter pattern | ECC já tem adapters; autofagia deve seguir mesma arquitetura |
159: | Documentar protocolos separadamente | ECC tem documentação própria robusta; protocolos devem complementar |
160: 
161: ## Issues Encountered
162: | Issue | Resolution |
163: |-------|------------|
164: | ECC tem 30+ hooks que podem conflitar | Usar hooks específicos de autofagia com prefixo `ecc-autofagia-` |
165: | Continuous learning v2 pode competir com autofagia | Autofagia opera em nível meta (analisar o sistema), não no mesmo nível |
166: | Cross-harness testing complexo | Focar em Claude Code + OpenCode como harnesses primários |
167:

169: - ECC Repo: https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC
170: - ECC Docs: https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/tree/main/docs
171: - Gran-Mestre: ~/.opencode/agent/gran-mestre.md
172: - Claude-Mem: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem
173: - Planning-with-Files: https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files

138:   artifacts:

151: **Also extract `must_haves.prohibitions`** when present (ADR-550 D3 — the must-NOT sibling block, distinct from `truths`). Each item is `{ statement, status, verification }` where `verification` is `test | judgment`. These are NEGATIVE checks: a verified prohibition means the must-NOT did NOT happen. Route them by verification tier in the verdict assembly (ADR-550 D4, the "B-with-guard" 2026-06-12 maintainer decision):
152: 
153: - **judgment-tier prohibitions → mode-dependent soft-gate.** Interactive verify requires explicit human resolution per item (belongs in the end-of-phase human checkpoint, not a mid-run gate). Autonomous verify records a NON-AUTHORITATIVE LLM-judge verdict plus a prominent `unverified-prohibition — human review recommended` flag in the verdict/SUMMARY — autonomous completion reads "complete with N flagged prohibitions". NEVER a silent pass; NEVER a hard halt of an AFK run.
154: - **test-tier prohibitions → FAIL CLOSED (accept-and-flag, not reject-at-parse).** Accept the `verification: test` value (the SPEC↔must_haves.prohibitions projection contract must hold, so no schema change is forced later). But a well-formed test-tier item that reaches verify with NO wired enforcement is treated as UNVERIFIED — flagged exactly like an unresolved judgment item, NEVER green. The deterministic fail-closed default is `dispositionForProhibition()` in probe-core (status `unverified`, `flagged: true` when `enforcementEvidence` is empty). Do NOT wire a real fail-first negative-test hard gate here — that enforcement MECHANISM defers to a follow-up PR (it needs a real test-tier consumer to `regression-must-fail-first` against; #644's corpus is entirely judgment-tier).
155: 
156: A flagged prohibition counts as a human-verification item (status `human_needed`) or a gap (status `gaps_found`) per the existing decision tree — it must never be silently absorbed into a `passed` verdict.

179: ## Step 3: Verify Observable Truths
180: 
181: For each truth, determine if codebase enables it.
182: 
183: **Verification status:**
184: 
185: - ✓ VERIFIED: All supporting artifacts pass all checks — and, for a behavior-dependent truth, a behavioral test exercises the asserted behavior (see below)
186: - ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED: Supporting artifacts are present and wired, but the truth asserts runtime behavior that no test exercises — present, not behaviorally proven. Routes to human verification (Step 8) and does NOT count toward the verified score (Step 9).
187: - ✗ FAILED: One or more artifacts missing, stub, or unwired
188: - ? UNCERTAIN: Can't verify programmatically (needs human)
189: 
190: **Behavior-dependent truths.** A truth is *behavior-dependent* when its correctness hinges on runtime behavior grep/presence checks cannot see — a **state transition** or a **cancellation / cleanup / ordering invariant** (e.g. "cancels the in-flight task and bumps the generation counter", "resets the busy flag on abort", "rolls back on failure"). For these, symbol presence + wiring is *necessary but not sufficient*: the code can be present and wired yet still leak state on the very path the invariant covers.
191: 
192: For each truth:
193: 
194: 1. Identify supporting artifacts
195: 2. Check artifact status (Step 4)
196: 3. Check wiring status (Step 5)
197: 4. **Before marking FAIL or PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED:** Check for override (Step 3b)
198: 5. **Classify behavior-dependence.** If the truth asserts a state transition or a cancellation/cleanup/ordering invariant, its status cannot be VERIFIED on presence alone:
199:    - A pre-existing test exercises the transition/invariant and passes (confirm via Step 7b's single-named-test path) → ✓ VERIFIED.
200:    - No such test exists, or it can't run without a server/state mutation → ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED. Emit a human-verification item (Step 8) and do not count it toward the verified score (Step 9).
201:    - An accepted override (Step 3b) carries the truth as PASSED (override), exactly as it does for a FAILED truth.
202: 6. Determine truth status
203: 
204: ## Step 3b: Check Verification Overrides
205: 
206: Before marking any must-have as FAILED or ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED, check the VERIFICATION.md frontmatter for an `overrides:` entry that matches this must-have.
207: 
208: **Override check procedure:**
209: 
210: 1. Parse `overrides:` array from VERIFICATION.md frontmatter (if present)
211: 2. For each override entry, normalize both the override `must_have` and the current truth to lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace
212: 3. Split into tokens and compute intersection — match if 80% token overlap in either direction
213: 4. Key technical terms (file paths, component names, API endpoints) have higher weight
214: 
215: **If override found:**
216: - Mark as `PASSED (override)` instead of FAIL/PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED
217: - Evidence: `Override: {reason} — accepted by {accepted_by} on {accepted_at}`
218: - Count toward passing score (`verified_truths`), not failing score
219: 
220: **If no override found:**
221: - Mark as FAILED (or ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED, per Step 3 step 5) as normal
222: - Consider suggesting an override if the failure looks intentional (alternative implementation exists)
223: 
224: **Suggesting overrides:** When a must-have FAILs but evidence shows an alternative implementation that achieves the same intent, include an override suggestion in the report:
225: 
226: ```markdown
227: **This looks intentional.** To accept this deviation, add to VERIFICATION.md frontmatter:
228: 
229: ```yaml
230: overrides:
231:   - must_have: "{must-have text}"
232:     reason: "{why this deviation is acceptable}"
233:     accepted_by: "{name}"
234:     accepted_at: "{ISO timestamp}"
235: ```
236: ```

238: ## Step 4: Verify Artifacts (Three Levels)
239: 
240: Use `gsd-tools query` for artifact verification against must_haves in PLAN frontmatter:
241: 
242: ```bash
243: ARTIFACT_RESULT=$(gsd_run query verify.artifacts "$PLAN_PATH")
244: ```
245: 
246: Parse JSON result: `{ all_passed, passed, total, artifacts: [{path, exists, issues, passed}] }`
247: 
248: For each artifact in result:
249: - `exists=false` → MISSING
250: - `issues` contains "Only N lines" or "Missing pattern" → STUB
251: - `passed=true` → VERIFIED
252: 
253: **Artifact status mapping:**
254: 
255: | exists | issues empty | Status      |
256: | ------ | ------------ | ----------- |
257: | true   | true         | ✓ VERIFIED  |
258: | true   | false        | ✗ STUB      |
259: | false  | -            | ✗ MISSING   |
260: 
261: **For wiring verification (Level 3)**, check imports/usage manually for artifacts that pass Levels 1-2:
262: 
263: ```bash
264: # Import check
265: grep -r "import.*$artifact_name" "${search_path:-src/}" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" 2>/dev/null | wc -l
266: 
267: # Usage check (beyond imports)
268: grep -r "$artifact_name" "${search_path:-src/}" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" 2>/dev/null | grep -v "import" | wc -l
269: ```
270: 
271: **Wiring status:**
272: - WIRED: Imported AND used
273: - ORPHANED: Exists but not imported/used
274: - PARTIAL: Imported but not used (or vice versa)
275: 
276: ### Final Artifact Status
277: 
278: | Exists | Substantive | Wired | Status      |
279: | ------ | ----------- | ----- | ----------- |
280: | ✓      | ✓           | ✓     | ✓ VERIFIED  |
281: | ✓      | ✓           | ✗     | ⚠️ ORPHANED |
282: | ✓      | ✗           | -     | ✗ STUB      |
283: | ✗      | -           | -     | ✗ MISSING   |

285: ## Step 4b: Data-Flow Trace (Level 4)
286: 
287: Artifacts that pass Levels 1-3 (exist, substantive, wired) can still be hollow if their data source produces empty or hardcoded values. Level 4 traces upstream from the artifact to verify real data flows through the wiring.
288: 
289: **When to run:** For each artifact that passes Level 3 (WIRED) and renders dynamic data (components, pages, dashboards — not utilities or configs).
290: 
291: **How:**
292: 
293: 1. **Identify the data variable** — what state/prop does the artifact render?
294: 
295: ```bash
296: # Find state variables that are rendered in JSX/TSX
297: grep -n -E "useState|useQuery|useSWR|useStore|props\." "$artifact" 2>/dev/null
298: ```
299: 
300: 2. **Trace the data source** — where does that variable get populated?
301: 
302: ```bash
303: # Find the fetch/query that populates the state
304: grep -n -A 5 "set${STATE_VAR}\|${STATE_VAR}\s*=" "$artifact" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "fetch|axios|query|store|dispatch|props\."
305: ```
306: 
307: 3. **Verify the source produces real data** — does the API/store return actual data or static/empty values?
308: 
309: ```bash
310: # Check the API route or data source for real DB queries vs static returns
311: grep -n -E "prisma\.|db\.|query\(|findMany|findOne|select|FROM" "$source_file" 2>/dev/null
312: # Flag: static returns with no query
313: grep -n -E "return.*json\(\s*\[\]|return.*json\(\s*\{\}" "$source_file" 2>/dev/null
314: ```
315: 
316: 4. **Check for disconnected props** — props passed to child components that are hardcoded empty at the call site
317: 
318: ```bash
319: # Find where the component is used and check prop values
320: grep -r -A 3 "<${COMPONENT_NAME}" "${search_path:-src/}" --include="*.tsx" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "=\{(\[\]|\{\}|null|''|\"\")\}"
321: ```
322: 
323: **Data-flow status:**
324: 
325: | Data Source | Produces Real Data | Status |
326: | ---------- | ------------------ | ------ |
327: | DB query found | Yes | ✓ FLOWING |
328: | Fetch exists, static fallback only | No | ⚠️ STATIC |
329: | No data source found | N/A | ✗ DISCONNECTED |
330: | Props hardcoded empty at call site | No | ✗ HOLLOW_PROP |
331: 
332: **Final Artifact Status (updated with Level 4):**
333: 
334: | Exists | Substantive | Wired | Data Flows | Status |
335: | ------ | ----------- | ----- | ---------- | ------ |
336: | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ VERIFIED |
337: | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ⚠️ HOLLOW — wired but data disconnected |
338: | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | - | ⚠️ ORPHANED |
339: | ✓ | ✗ | - | - | ✗ STUB |
340: | ✗ | - | - | - | ✗ MISSING |

342: ## Step 5: Verify Key Links (Wiring)
343: 
344: Key links are critical connections. If broken, the goal fails even with all artifacts present.
345: 
346: Use `gsd-tools query` for key link verification against must_haves in PLAN frontmatter:
347: 
348: ```bash
349: LINKS_RESULT=$(gsd_run query verify.key-links "$PLAN_PATH")
350: ```
351: 
352: Parse JSON result: `{ all_verified, verified, total, links: [{from, to, via, verified, detail}] }`
353: 
354: For each link:
355: - `verified=true` → WIRED
356: - `verified=false` with "not found" in detail → NOT_WIRED
357: - `verified=false` with "Pattern not found" → PARTIAL
358: 
359: **Fallback patterns** (if must_haves.key_links not defined in PLAN):
360: 
361: ### Pattern: Component → API
362: 
363: ```bash
364: grep -E "fetch\(['\"].*$api_path|axios\.(get|post).*$api_path" "$component" 2>/dev/null
365: grep -A 5 "fetch\|axios" "$component" | grep -E "await|\.then|setData|setState" 2>/dev/null
366: ```
367: 
368: Status: WIRED (call + response handling) | PARTIAL (call, no response use) | NOT_WIRED (no call)
369: 
370: ### Pattern: API → Database
371: 
372: ```bash
373: grep -E "prisma\.$model|db\.$model|$model\.(find|create|update|delete)" "$route" 2>/dev/null
374: grep -E "return.*json.*\w+|res\.json\(\w+" "$route" 2>/dev/null
375: ```
376: 
377: Status: WIRED (query + result returned) | PARTIAL (query, static return) | NOT_WIRED (no query)
378: 
379: ### Pattern: Form → Handler
380: 
381: ```bash
382: grep -E "onSubmit=\{|handleSubmit" "$component" 2>/dev/null
383: grep -A 10 "onSubmit.*=" "$component" | grep -E "fetch|axios|mutate|dispatch" 2>/dev/null
384: ```
385: 
386: Status: WIRED (handler + API call) | STUB (only logs/preventDefault) | NOT_WIRED (no handler)
387: 
388: ### Pattern: State → Render
389: 
390: ```bash
391: grep -E "useState.*$state_var|\[$state_var," "$component" 2>/dev/null
392: grep -E "\{.*$state_var.*\}|\{$state_var\." "$component" 2>/dev/null
393: ```
394: 
395: Status: WIRED (state displayed) | NOT_WIRED (state exists, not rendered)

451: # Empty implementations
452: grep -n -E "return null|return \{\}|return \[\]|=> \{\}" "$file" 2>/dev/null
453: # Hardcoded empty data (common stub patterns)
454: grep -n -E "=\s*\[\]|=\s*\{\}|=\s*null|=\s*undefined" "$file" 2>/dev/null | grep -v -E "(test|spec|mock|fixture|\.test\.|\.spec\.)" 2>/dev/null
455: # Props with hardcoded empty values (React/Vue/Svelte stub indicators)
456: grep -n -E "=\{(\[\]|\{\}|null|undefined|''|\"\")\}" "$file" 2>/dev/null
457: # Console.log only implementations
458: grep -n -B 2 -A 2 "console\.log" "$file" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^\s*(const|function|=>)"
459: ```
460: 
461: **Stub classification:** A grep match is a STUB only when the value flows to rendering or user-visible output AND no other code path populates it with real data. A test helper, type default, or initial state that gets overwritten by a fetch/store is NOT a stub. Check for data-fetching (useEffect, fetch, query, useSWR, useQuery, subscribe) that writes to the same variable before flagging.
462: 
463: **Debt marker gate:** Any `TBD`, `FIXME`, or `XXX` marker in a file modified by this phase is a 🛑 BLOCKER unless the same line references formal follow-up work (`issue #123`, `PR #123`, `#123`, or `DEF-*`). Unreferenced markers mean completion is not auditable; set `status: gaps_found` and list each marker under `gaps`.
464: 
465: Categorize: 🛑 Blocker (prevents goal or unresolved debt marker) | ⚠️ Warning (incomplete) | ℹ️ Info (notable)
466: 
467: ## Step 7b: Behavioral Spot-Checks
468: 
469: Anti-pattern scanning (Step 7) checks for code smells. Behavioral spot-checks go further — they verify that key behaviors actually produce expected output when invoked.
470: 
471: **When to run:** For phases that produce runnable code (APIs, CLI tools, build scripts, data pipelines). Skip for documentation-only or config-only phases.
472: 
473: **Behavioral evidence for behavior-dependent truths (Step 3).** When a truth asserts a state transition or a cancellation/cleanup/ordering invariant, the single named test below is what upgrades it from ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED to ✓ VERIFIED. Run only the one named test that exercises the transition/invariant — never the full suite (per #25/#753). If no such test exists, leave the truth ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED and route it to human verification (Step 8); do not mark it VERIFIED on presence.
474: 
475: **How:**
476: 
477: 1. **Identify checkable behaviors** from must-haves truths. Select 2-4 that can be tested with a single command:
478: 
479: ```bash
480: # API endpoint returns non-empty data
481: curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/api/$ENDPOINT 2>/dev/null | node -e "let b='';process.stdin.setEncoding('utf8');process.stdin.on('data',c=>b+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{const d=JSON.parse(b);process.exit(Array.isArray(d)?(d.length>0?0:1):(Object.keys(d).length>0?0:1))})"
482: 
483: # CLI command produces expected output
484: node $CLI_PATH --help 2>&1 | grep -q "$EXPECTED_SUBCOMMAND"
485: 
486: # Build produces output files
487: ls $BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR/*.{js,css} 2>/dev/null | wc -l
488: 
489: # Module exports expected functions
490: node -e "const m = require('$MODULE_PATH'); console.log(typeof m.$FUNCTION_NAME)" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "function"
491: 
492: # A test EXISTS (existence proof — enumerate, do NOT run the suite)
493: cargo test -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$PHASE_TEST_PATTERN"   # pytest --collect-only -q · npx vitest list · go test -list '.*'
494: 
495: # A specific test PASSES (run ONE named test, never the whole suite)
496: cargo test "$TEST_NAME" -- --exact   # pytest -k "$TEST_NAME" · npx vitest run -t "$TEST_NAME"
497: ```
498: 
499: 2. **Run each check** and record pass/fail:
500: 
501: **Spot-check status:**
502: 
503: | Behavior | Command | Result | Status |
504: | -------- | ------- | ------ | ------ |
505: | {truth} | {command} | {output} | ✓ PASS / ✗ FAIL / ? SKIP |
506: 
507: 3. **Classification:**
508:    - ✓ PASS: Command succeeded and output matches expected
509:    - ✗ FAIL: Command failed or output is empty/wrong — flag as gap
510:    - ? SKIP: Can't test without running server/external service — route to human verification (Step 8)
511: 
512: **Spot-check constraints:**
513: - Each check must complete in under 10 seconds
514: - Do not start servers or services — only test what's already runnable
515: - Do not modify state (no writes, no mutations, no side effects)
516: - **Run the full workspace test command at most once per verification.** Never filter a full run per must-have (`<full-suite> 2>&1 | grep X` repeated per truth) — it re-runs everything and yields no new evidence. Prove a test exists by enumeration (`--list` / `--collect-only`); prove one passes via a single named test. If a full run is genuinely required, run it once and `grep` the saved output.
517: - If the project has no runnable entry points yet, skip with: "Step 7b: SKIPPED (no runnable entry points)"
518: 
519: ## Step 7c: Probe Execution
520: 
521: SUMMARY.md probe pass claims are not evidence. If a phase declares or implies probe-based verification, the verifier must run the probe in its own process and record the command result.
522: 
523: **When to run:** For migration phases, CLI/tooling phases, or any phase whose PLAN/SUMMARY/verification criteria mention probes, PASS markers, stage markers, runnable checks, or `scripts/*/tests/probe-*.sh`.
524: 
525: **Probe discovery:**
526: 
527: ```bash
528: # Conventional project probes
529: find scripts -path '*/tests/probe-*.sh' -type f 2>/dev/null | sort
530: 
531: # Phase-declared probes
532: grep -R -n -E 'probe-[^[:space:]]+\.sh|scripts/.*/tests/probe-.*\.sh' "$PHASE_DIR"/*-PLAN.md "$PHASE_DIR"/*-SUMMARY.md 2>/dev/null
533: ```
534: 
535: **Execution contract:**
536: 
537: 1. Build the `PROBES` list from explicit PLAN declarations first; include conventional `scripts/*/tests/probe-*.sh` when the phase is a migration/tooling phase or the success criteria mention probes.
538: 2. For every documented probe path, if the file is missing or unreadable, mark `MISSING_PROBE` and set `status: gaps_found`. Do not require the executable bit because probes run through `bash "$probe"`.
539: 3. Run each probe from the built `PROBES` list (declared + conventional) from the repository root:
540: 
541: ```bash
542: for probe in "${PROBES[@]}"; do
543:   timeout 30s bash "$probe"
544: done
545: ```
546: 
547: 4. Exit code 0 is PASS. Any non-zero exit is FAILED and must include stdout/stderr evidence in VERIFICATION.md.
548: 5. Do not substitute executor narration, SUMMARY.md PASS-marker counts, or a different dry-run driver command for the probe result.
549: 
550: **Probe status:**
551: 
552: | Probe | Command | Result | Status |
553: | ----- | ------- | ------ | ------ |
554: | `scripts/.../probe-name.sh` | `bash "$probe"` | exit code/output | PASS / FAILED / MISSING_PROBE |

556: ## Step 8: Identify Human Verification Needs
557: 
558: **Always needs human:** Visual appearance, user flow completion, real-time behavior, external service integration, performance feel, error message clarity.
559: 
560: **Needs human if uncertain:** Complex wiring grep can't trace, dynamic state behavior, edge cases.
561: 
562: **Behavior-unverified truths (Step 3):** Every truth left ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED is recorded in the `behavior_unverified_items` frontmatter list (emitted whenever the count > 0, regardless of overall status, so it survives a gaps_found phase) and surfaces for human verification; when the overall status is human_needed it also appears in the human_verification section. Phrase each item around the invariant: what to trigger, what state must hold afterward, and why presence checks can't see it.
563: 
564: **Harvest deferred items from PLAN.md (#3309 / `workflow.human_verify_mode = end-of-phase`):** Scan every PLAN file in the phase for `<verify><human-check>` blocks on `auto` tasks. These are verification items the planner deliberately deferred from `checkpoint:human-verify` to end-of-phase to avoid the executor cold-start cost. Each block has the same shape used by the planner:
565: 
566: ```xml
567: <verify>
568:   <human-check>
569:     <test>What to do</test>
570:     <expected>What should happen</expected>
571:     <why_human>Why grep can't verify</why_human>
572:   </human-check>
573: </verify>
574: ```
575: 
576: Merge those harvested items into the same human verification list as your own analysis. Deduplicate when the planner-deferred item and your own analysis describe the same check. The downstream `human_needed` → `{phase_num}-UAT.md` path in `workflows/execute-phase.md` is the single sink — no separate file is created.
577: 
578: **Format:**
579: 
580: ```markdown
581: ### 1. {Test Name}
582: 
583: **Test:** {What to do}
584: **Expected:** {What should happen}
585: **Why human:** {Why can't verify programmatically}
586: ```

588: ## Step 9: Determine Overall Status
589: 
590: Classify status using this decision tree IN ORDER (most restrictive first):
591: 
592: 1. IF any truth FAILED, artifact MISSING/STUB, key link NOT_WIRED, or blocker anti-pattern found:
593:    → **status: gaps_found**
594: 
595: 2. IF Step 8 produced ANY human verification items (section is non-empty) — this includes every ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED truth from Step 3:
596:    → **status: human_needed**
597:    (Even if all other truths are VERIFIED — human items take priority)
598: 
599: 3. IF all truths VERIFIED, all artifacts pass, all links WIRED, no blockers, AND no human verification items:
600:    → **status: passed**
601: 
602: **passed is ONLY valid when the human verification section is empty.** If Step 8 produced any items — including any truth left ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED — the status is not `passed`: it is `human_needed`, or `gaps_found` when rule 1 also fires (the ordered tree keeps gaps_found's precedence).
603: 
604: **A ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED truth is never FAILED and never VERIFIED.** It does not trigger gaps_found (the code is present and wired) and is not counted as verified (behavior unexercised). On its own it routes to human_needed; when a higher-precedence gaps_found also applies, the status stays gaps_found and the item is preserved in the always-on `behavior_unverified_items` list so it is never lost. Either way it stays a *per-truth* state — the overall-status vocabulary is unchanged, with no new status value.
605: 
606: > **Shared status seam**: the status vocabulary (`passed`, `gaps_found`, `human_needed`) and the per-status routing (next action and next command for each value) are owned by `src/verification.cts` via `gsd_run query verification.status`. This agent is the single emitter of the frontmatter status field; consumers (ship.md, execute-phase.md) read routing from that query instead of re-deriving it.
607: 
608: **Score (presence- vs behavior-verified split):**
609: 
610: - `verified_truths` counts ✓ VERIFIED truths plus PASSED (override) truths (Step 3b). For a behavior-dependent truth, VERIFIED means a behavioral test passed, not just that symbols are present.
611: - ⚠️ PRESENT_BEHAVIOR_UNVERIFIED truths are the *only* ones excluded from `verified_truths`; they are reported separately as `behavior_unverified`.
612: 
613: ```text
614: score: verified_truths / total_truths        # e.g. 6/7
615: behavior_unverified: P                        # truths present + wired but behavior not exercised
616: ```
617: 
618: A headline N/N therefore certifies that every behavior-dependent truth had behavioral evidence — a clean score can no longer be reached on symbol presence alone.
619: 
620: ## Step 9b: Filter Deferred Items
621: 
622: Before reporting gaps, check if any identified gaps are explicitly addressed in later phases of the current milestone. This prevents false-positive gap reports for items intentionally scheduled for future work.
623: 
624: **Load the full milestone roadmap:**
625: 
626: ```bash
627: ROADMAP_DATA=$(gsd_run query roadmap.analyze --raw)
628: ```
629: 
630: Parse the JSON to extract all phases. Identify phases with `number > current_phase_number` (later phases in the milestone). For each later phase, extract its `goal` and `success_criteria`.
631: 
632: **For each potential gap identified in Step 9:**
633: 
634: 1. Check if the gap's failed truth or missing item is covered by a later phase's goal or success criteria
635: 2. **Match criteria:** The gap's concern appears in a later phase's goal text, success criteria text, or the later phase's name clearly suggests it covers this area of work
636: 3. If a match is found → move the gap to the `deferred` list, recording which phase addresses it and the matching evidence (goal text or success criterion)
637: 4. If the gap does not match any later phase → keep it as a real `gap`
638: 
639: **Important:** Be conservative when matching. Only defer a gap when there is clear, specific evidence in a later phase's roadmap section. Vague or tangential matches should NOT cause a gap to be deferred — when in doubt, keep it as a real gap.
640: 
641: **Deferred items do NOT affect the status determination.** After filtering, recalculate:
642: 
643: - If the gaps list is now empty and no human verification items exist → `passed`
644: - If the gaps list is now empty but human verification items exist → `human_needed`
645: - If the gaps list still has items → `gaps_found`

688: ## MVP Mode Verification
689: 
690: **When the phase under verification has `mode: mvp` in ROADMAP.md (resolved by the verify-work workflow):** Apply the goal-backward methodology, narrowed to the phase's user-story goal. Required reading: `@$HOME/.claude/gsd-core/references/verify-mvp-mode.md`.
691: 
692: **Core narrowing rule:** Goal-backward verification normally checks that the phase goal is observably true in the codebase. Under MVP mode, the phase goal IS a user story ("As a [user role], I want to [capability], so that [outcome]."). Verify the `[outcome]` clause is observably true — that is the success condition.
693: 
694: **VERIFICATION.md output structure under MVP mode:**
695: 
696: 1. Top-level "User Flow Coverage" table: each step of the user story → expected → evidence in codebase → status. (Format defined in `references/verify-mvp-mode.md`.)
697: 2. Standard technical-check sections (API verification, error handling, etc.) follow below — only if the user flow coverage is complete.
698: 
699: **User Story format guard:** Apply via the centralized verb instead of inlining the regex:
700: 
701: ```bash
702: USER_STORY_VALID=$(gsd_run query user-story.validate --story "$PHASE_GOAL" --pick valid)
703: ```
704: 
705: If `valid != true`, refuse to verify. Surface the discrepancy and ask the user to run `/gsd mvp-phase ${PHASE}` to set a proper User Story goal. The verb owns the canonical regex `/^As a .+, I want to .+, so that .+\.$/` and surfaces per-error guidance in `errors[]` plus slot extractions in `slots`. Do NOT attempt to verify against a non-User Story goal under MVP mode — the User Flow Coverage section would be low-quality.
706: 
707: **Mode is all-or-nothing per phase** (PRD decision Q1, inherited from Phase 1). The MVP Mode Verification rules apply to the whole phase or not at all.
708: 
709: **Compatibility with existing verifier behavior:** When the phase mode is null/absent, this section is dormant. The existing goal-backward verification methodology is unchanged for non-MVP phases.

216: **When `workflow.tdd_mode` is enabled:** Apply TDD heuristics aggressively — all eligible tasks MUST use `type: tdd`. Read @$HOME/.claude/gsd-core/references/tdd.md for gate enforcement rules and the end-of-phase review checkpoint format.

218: **When `workflow.tdd_mode` is disabled (default):** Apply TDD heuristics opportunistically — use `type: tdd` only when the benefit is clear.

224: **TDD candidates (dedicated TDD plans):** Business logic with defined I/O, API endpoints with request/response contracts, data transformations, validation rules, algorithms, state machines.

228: **Why TDD gets own plan:** TDD requires RED→GREEN→REFACTOR cycles consuming 40-50% context. Embedding in multi-task plans degrades quality.

453: ## Goal-Backward Methodology
454: 
455: **Forward planning:** "What should we build?" → produces tasks.

458: ## The Process
459: 
460: **Step 0: Extract Requirement IDs**
461: Read ROADMAP.md `**Requirements:**` line for this phase. Strip brackets if present (e.g., `[AUTH-01, AUTH-02]` → `AUTH-01, AUTH-02`). Distribute requirement IDs across plans — each plan's `requirements` frontmatter field MUST list the IDs its tasks address. **CRITICAL:** Every requirement ID MUST appear in at least one plan. Plans with an empty `requirements` field are invalid.
462: 
463: **Security (when `security_enforcement` enabled — absent = enabled):** Identify trust boundaries in this phase's scope. Map STRIDE categories to applicable tech stack from RESEARCH.md security domain. For each threat: assign a **severity** (critical|high|medium|low) based on impact × likelihood, and a disposition (`mitigate`/`accept`/`transfer`) per the configured OWASP ASVS level — see @$HOME/.claude/gsd-core/references/security-asvs-levels.md. Every plan MUST include `<threat_model>` when security_enforcement is enabled.
464: 
465: **Package legitimacy gate (npm/pip/cargo only):**
466: - Require RESEARCH.md `## Package Legitimacy Audit` before package-manager install tasks.
467: - If install tasks exist and the table is missing/malformed, stop planning:

494: <checkpoints>
495: 
496: ## Checkpoint Types
497: 
498: **checkpoint:human-verify (90% of checkpoints)**
499: Human confirms Claude's automated work works correctly.
500: 
501: Use for: Visual UI checks, interactive flows, functional verification, animation/accessibility.
502: 
503: ```xml
504: <task type="checkpoint:human-verify" gate="blocking">
505:   <what-built>[What Claude automated]</what-built>
506:   <how-to-verify>
507:     [Exact steps to test - URLs, commands, expected behavior]
508:   </how-to-verify>
509:   <resume-signal>Type "approved" or describe issues</resume-signal>
510: </task>
511: ```
512: 
513: **checkpoint:decision (9% of checkpoints)**
514: Human makes implementation choice affecting direction.
515: 
516: Use for: Technology selection, architecture decisions, design choices.
517: 
518: ```xml
519: <task type="checkpoint:decision" gate="blocking">
520:   <decision>[What's being decided]</decision>
521:   <context>[Why this matters]</context>
522:   <options>
523:     <option id="option-a">
524:       <name>[Name]</name>
525:       <pros>[Benefits]</pros>
526:       <cons>[Tradeoffs]</cons>
527:     </option>
528:   </options>
529:   <resume-signal>Select: option-a, option-b, or ...</resume-signal>
530: </task>
531: ```
532: 
533: **checkpoint:human-action (1% - rare)**
534: Action has NO CLI/API and requires human-only interaction.
535: 
536: Use ONLY for: Email verification links, SMS 2FA codes, manual account approvals, credit card 3D Secure flows.
537: 
538: Do NOT use for: Deploying (use CLI), creating webhooks (use API), creating databases (use provider CLI), running builds/tests (use Bash), creating files (use Write).
539: 
540: ## Authentication Gates
541: 
542: When Claude tries CLI/API and gets auth error → creates checkpoint → user authenticates → Claude retries. Auth gates are created dynamically, NOT pre-planned.
543: 
544: ## Writing Guidelines
545: 
546: **DO:** Automate everything before checkpoint, be specific ("Visit https://myapp.vercel.app" not "check deployment"), number verification steps, state expected outcomes.
547: 
548: **DON'T:** Ask human to do work Claude can automate, mix multiple verifications, place checkpoints before automation completes.
549:

551: 
552: For checkpoint anti-patterns, specificity comparison tables, context section anti-patterns, and scope reduction patterns:
553: @$HOME/.claude/gsd-core/references/planner-antipatterns.md

557: <tdd_integration>
558: 
559: ## TDD Plan Structure
560: 
561: TDD candidates identified in task_breakdown get dedicated plans (type: tdd). One feature per TDD plan.
562: 
563: ```markdown
564: ---
565: phase: XX-name
566: plan: NN
567: type: tdd
568: ---
569: 
570: <objective>
571: [What feature and why]
572: Purpose: [Design benefit of TDD for this feature]
573: Output: [Working, tested feature]
574: </objective>
575: 
576: <feature>
577:   <name>[Feature name]</name>
578:   <files>[source file, test file]</files>
579:   <behavior>
580:     [Expected behavior in testable terms]
581:     Cases: input -> expected output
582:   </behavior>
583:   <implementation>[How to implement once tests pass]</implementation>
584: </feature>
585: ```
586: 
587: ## Red-Green-Refactor Cycle
588: 
589: **RED:** Create test file → write test describing expected behavior → run test (MUST fail) → commit: `test({phase}-{plan}): add failing test for [feature]`
590: 
591: **GREEN:** Write minimal code to pass → run test (MUST pass) → commit: `feat({phase}-{plan}): implement [feature]`
592: 
593: **REFACTOR (if needed):** Clean up → run tests (MUST pass) → commit: `refactor({phase}-{plan}): clean up [feature]`
594: 
595: Each TDD plan produces 2-3 atomic commits.
596: 
597: ## Context Budget for TDD
598: 
599: TDD plans target ~40% context (lower than standard 50%). The RED→GREEN→REFACTOR back-and-forth with file reads, test runs, and output analysis is heavier than linear execution.
600: 
601: </tdd_integration>

786: <step name="assign_waves">
787: ```
788: waves = {}
789: for each plan in plan_order:
790:   if plan.depends_on is empty:

792:   else:
793:     plan.wave = max(waves[dep] for dep in plan.depends_on) + 1
794:   waves[plan.id] = plan.wave
795: 
796: # Implicit dependency: files_modified overlap forces a later wave.
797: for each plan B in plan_order:
798:   for each earlier plan A where A != B:
799:     if any file in B.files_modified is also in A.files_modified:
800:       B.wave = max(B.wave, A.wave + 1)
801:       waves[B.id] = B.wave
802: ```
803: 
804: **Rule:** Same-wave plans must have zero `files_modified` overlap. After assigning waves, scan each wave; if any file appears in 2+ plans, bump the later plan to the next wave and repeat.

841: <step name="write_phase_prompt">

844: **ALWAYS use the Write tool to create files** — never use `Bash(cat << 'EOF')` or heredoc commands for file creation.
845: 
846: **Write contract (hard rules — must follow):**
847: 
848: These PLAN.md files are the canonical output of this agent. The orchestrator reads each `.planning/phases/{padded_phase}-{slug}/{padded_phase}-{NN}-PLAN.md` from disk after you return; it does NOT read your return message for the file content.
849: 
850: **Write is for net-new PLAN.md only.** For any existing file (`ROADMAP.md`, `.planning/` files) use `Edit` (scoped replacement), never `Write`. See `update_roadmap`.
851: 
852: 1. **Default: write each PLAN.md in a single `Write` call.** On most runtimes this is correct and reliable — do this unless rule 4 applies.
853: 2. **Do NOT return the PLAN.md content in your response.** Your return message is a brief confirmation (see `<structured_returns>`); the content lives on disk.
854: 3. **Do NOT use `Bash(cat << 'EOF')` or heredoc** for file creation. Use the `Write` tool.
855: 4. **Large-file / truncation fallback.** Some runtimes (e.g. OpenCode) cap tool-call output, and a single oversized `Write` is truncated mid-payload — surfacing a tool error such as `JSON Parse error: Expected '}'`. If a `Write` fails with a truncation / invalid-tool error, **do NOT retry the same oversized call** (that loops forever). Instead build the file incrementally so no single tool call carries the whole payload:
856:    - `Write` the file with only the first section, ending with the sentinel line `<!-- gsd:write-continue -->`.
857:    - `Read` the file, then `Edit` it, replacing `<!-- gsd:write-continue -->` with the next section followed by the sentinel again. Repeat, one section per `Edit`.
858:    - On the final section, replace the sentinel with the closing content and no trailing sentinel.
859: 5. **If writing still fails, surface the actual error in your return message.** **Do NOT silently fall back to returning content** — that hides the failure from the orchestrator and truncates identically.
860: 
861: **CRITICAL — File naming convention (enforced):**
862: 
863: The filename MUST follow the exact pattern: `{padded_phase}-{NN}-PLAN.md`
864: 
865: - `{padded_phase}` = zero-padded phase number received from the orchestrator (e.g. `01`, `02`, `03`, `02.1`)
866: - `{NN}` = zero-padded sequential plan number within the phase (e.g. `01`, `02`, `03`)
867: - The suffix is always `-PLAN.md` — NEVER `PLAN-NN.md`, `NN-PLAN.md`, or any other variation
868: 
869: **Correct examples:**
870: - Phase 1, Plan 1 → `01-01-PLAN.md`
871: - Phase 3, Plan 2 → `03-02-PLAN.md`
872: - Phase 2.1, Plan 1 → `02.1-01-PLAN.md`
873: 
874: **Incorrect (will break GSD plan filename conventions / tooling detection):**
875: - ❌ `PLAN-01-auth.md`
876: - ❌ `01-PLAN-01.md`
877: - ❌ `plan-01.md`
878: - ❌ `01-01-plan.md` (lowercase)
879: 
880: Full write path: `.planning/phases/{padded_phase}-{slug}/{padded_phase}-{NN}-PLAN.md`
881: 
882: Include all frontmatter fields.

8:  * Hook Event Mapping:
9:  * - PreToolUse → tool.execute.before
10:  * - PostToolUse → tool.execute.after
11:  * - Stop → session.idle / session.status

13:  * - SessionEnd → session.deleted

76:   $,

82:   const worktreePath = worktree || directory

97:     }
98:   }

100:   const pendingToolChanges = new Map<string, { path: string; type: "added" | "modified" }>()
101:   let writeCounter = 0
102: 
103:   function getFilePath(args: ToolArgs | undefined): string | null {
104:     if (!args) return null

106:     return typeof p === "string" && p.trim() ? p : null
107:   }
108: 
109:   // Helper to call the SDK's log API with correct signature
110:   const log = (level: "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error", message: string) =>
111:     client.app.log({ body: { service: "ecc", level, message } })

113:   const normalizeProfile = (value: string | undefined): HookProfile => {

1: // graphify OpenCode plugin
2: // Injects a knowledge graph reminder before bash tool calls when the graph exists.
3: //
4: // IMPORTANT: keep the reminder string free of backticks and $(...) constructs.
5: // The hook prepends `echo "<reminder>" && <cmd>` to the user's bash command;
6: // backticks inside the double-quoted echo trigger bash command substitution,
7: // which both corrupts tool output and silently executes the very graphify
8: // command we are only suggesting. Plain words render fine in opencode's TUI.
9: import { existsSync } from "fs";
10: import { join } from "path";
11: 
12: export const GraphifyPlugin = async ({ directory }) => {
13:   let reminded = false;
14: 
15:   return {
16:     "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {
17:       if (reminded) return;
18:       if (!existsSync(join(directory, "graphify-out", "graph.json"))) return;
19: 
20:       if (input.tool === "bash") {
21:         // ';' not '&&' — Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejects '&&' as a statement
22:         // separator, breaking the first bash command of the session (#1646).
23:         output.args.command =
24:           'echo "[graphify] knowledge graph at graphify-out/. For focused questions, run graphify query with your question (scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md) instead of grepping raw files. Read GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad architecture context." ; ' +
25:           output.args.command;
26:         reminded = true;
27:       }
28:     },
29:   };
30: };

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """
3: OCR Pipeline para OpenCode — "Olhos" do Agente
4: Extrai texto de PDFs, imagens e documentos via Tesseract OCR + pdftotext.
5: Gera índice JSON pesquisável e atualiza notas .md com conteúdo extraído.
6: 
7: Uso:
8:     python3 ocr_extract.py                    # Processa todo o vault
9:     python3 ocr_extract.py --file <arquivo>   # Processa um arquivo específico
10:     python3 ocr_extract.py --query <texto>    # Busca no índice de extrações
11:     python3 ocr_extract.py --rebuild           # Reconstrói o índice completo
12: """
13: 
14: import os
15: import sys
16: import json
17: import hashlib
18: import subprocess
19: import argparse
20: import re
21: from pathlib import Path
22: from datetime import datetime
23: from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed
24: 
25: # Configurações
26: VAULT_PATH = Path("/mnt/dados/cerebro com IA")
27: SOURCE_PATH = Path("/mnt/win2/textos, pdf e esquemas")
28: EXTRACTS_DIR = VAULT_PATH / "textos, pdf e esquemas" / ".ocr-extracts"
29: INDEX_FILE = EXTRACTS_DIR / "ocr-index.json"
30: LOG_FILE = EXTRACTS_DIR / "ocr-log.txt"
31: 
32: # Tipos suportados
33: PDF_EXTS = {'.pdf'}
34: IMAGE_EXTS = {'.jpg', '.jpeg', '.png', '.gif', '.bmp', '.tiff', '.tif', '.webp'}
35: TEXT_EXTS = {'.txt', '.md', '.csv'}
36: ALL_EXTS = PDF_EXTS | IMAGE_EXTS | TEXT_EXTS
37: 
38: # Configuração Tesseract
39: TESSDATA = os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/tessdata")
40: os.environ["TESSDATA_PREFIX"] = os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share")
41: 
42: 
43: def log(msg, level="INFO"):
44:     timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
45:     line = f"[{timestamp}] [{level}] {msg}"
46:     print(line)
47:     with open(LOG_FILE, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
48:         f.write(line + "\n")
49: 
50: 
51: def file_hash(filepath):
52:     """Gera hash MD5 do arquivo para detectar mudanças."""
53:     h = hashlib.md5()
54:     with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
55:         for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(8192), b""):
56:             h.update(chunk)
57:     return h.hexdigest()
58: 
59: 
60: def extract_text_pdftotext(pdf_path):
61:     """Extrai texto de PDF usando pdftotext (poppler)."""
62:     try:
63:         result = subprocess.run(
64:             ["pdftotext", "-layout", str(pdf_path), "-"],
65:             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120,
66:             env={**os.environ, "TESSDATA_PREFIX": TESSDATA}
67:         )
68:         text = result.stdout.strip()
69:         if text and len(text) > 10:
70:             return text
71:     except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, Exception) as e:
72:         log(f"pdftotext falhou para {pdf_path}: {e}", "WARN")
73:     return None
74: 
75: 
76: def extract_text_tesseract(image_path):
77:     """Extrai texto de imagem usando Tesseract OCR."""
78:     try:
79:         result = subprocess.run(
80:             ["tesseract", str(image_path), "stdout", "-l", "por+eng", "--psm", "3"],
81:             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120,
82:             env={**os.environ, "TESSDATA_PREFIX": TESSDATA}
83:         )
84:         text = result.stdout.strip()
85:         if text and len(text) > 5:
86:             return text
87:     except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, Exception) as e:
88:         log(f"Tesseract falhou para {image_path}: {e}", "WARN")
89:     return None
90: 
91: 
92: def extract_text_from_pdf_with_ocr(pdf_path):
93:     """Extrai texto de PDF: tenta pdftotext primeiro, depois OCR página por página."""
94:     # Tentar pdftotext primeiro
95:     text = extract_text_pdftotext(pdf_path)
96:     if text and len(text) > 50:
97:         return text, "pdftotext"
98: 
99:     # Fallback: converter PDF para imagens e usar OCR
100:     try:
101:         tmp_dir = Path("/tmp/ocr_tmp")
102:         tmp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
103: 
104:         prefix = tmp_dir / f"page_{hashlib.md5(str(pdf_path).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}"
105: 
106:         subprocess.run(
107:             ["pdftoppm", "-r", "300", "-png", str(pdf_path), str(prefix)],
108:             capture_output=True, timeout=300,
109:             env={**os.environ, "TESSDATA_PREFIX": TESSDATA}
110:         )
111: 
112:         pages = sorted(tmp_dir.glob(f"{prefix.name}-*.png"))
113:         if not pages:
114:             # Tentar sem hífen
115:             pages = sorted(tmp_dir.glob(f"{prefix.name}*.png"))
116: 
117:         ocr_texts = []
118:         for page_img in pages:
119:             page_text = extract_text_tesseract(page_img)
120:             if page_text:
121:                 ocr_texts.append(page_text)
122:             page_img.unlink(missing_ok=True)
123: 
124:         if ocr_texts:
125:             return "\n\n".join(ocr_texts), "ocr-pdf"
126: 
127:     except Exception as e:
128:         log(f"OCR PDF falhou para {pdf_path}: {e}", "WARN")
129: 
130:     return None, None
131: 
132: 
133: def extract_text_plain(txt_path):
134:     """Lê arquivo de texto plano."""
135:     try:
136:         encodings = ['utf-8', 'latin-1', 'cp1252', 'iso-8859-1']
137:         for enc in encodings:
138:             try:
139:                 with open(txt_path, 'r', encoding=enc) as f:
140:                     return f.read(), "plain-text"
141:             except UnicodeDecodeError:
142:                 continue
143:     except Exception as e:
144:         log(f"Leitura falhou para {txt_path}: {e}", "WARN")
145:     return None, None
146:

148: def process_file(filepath):
149:     """Processa um arquivo individual e retorna dados de extração."""
150:     filepath = Path(filepath)
151:     ext = filepath.suffix.lower()
152: 
153:     # Caminho relativo ao vault
154:     try:
155:         rel_path = filepath.relative_to(VAULT_PATH)
156:     except ValueError:
157:         rel_path = filepath.relative_to(SOURCE_PATH)
158: 
159:     # Hash do arquivo
160:     fhash = file_hash(filepath)
161: 
162:     # Extrair texto conforme tipo
163:     text = None
164:     method = None
165: 
166:     if ext in PDF_EXTS:
167:         text, method = extract_text_from_pdf_with_ocr(filepath)
168:     elif ext in IMAGE_EXTS:
169:         text, method = extract_text_tesseract(filepath), "ocr-image"
170:     elif ext in TEXT_EXTS:
171:         text, method = extract_text_plain(filepath)
172: 
173:     if text and len(text) > 5:
174:         # Criar diretório de extrações
175:         extract_dir = EXTRACTS_DIR / rel_path.parent
176:         extract_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
177: 
178:         # Salvar texto extraído
179:         extract_file = extract_dir / f"{filepath.stem}.extracted.txt"
180:         with open(extract_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
181:             f.write(text)
182: 
183:         # Atualizar nota .md correspondente se existir
184:         md_file = filepath.parent / f"{filepath.stem}.md"
185:         if md_file.exists() and ext in PDF_EXTS | IMAGE_EXTS:
186:             update_md_with_extract(md_file, text, method)
187: 
188:         return {
189:             "path": str(rel_path),
190:             "hash": fhash,
191:             "method": method,
192:             "text_length": len(text),
193:             "preview": text[:500],
194:             "extracted_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
195:             "has_text": True
196:         }
197: 
198:     return {
199:         "path": str(rel_path),
200:         "hash": fhash,
201:         "method": method,
202:         "text_length": 0,
203:         "preview": "",
204:         "extracted_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
205:         "has_text": False
206:     }
207: 
208: 
209: def update_md_with_extract(md_file, text, method):
210:     """Atualiza nota .md com o texto extraído."""
211:     try:
212:         content = md_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
213: 
214:         # Se já tem seção de extração, substituir
215:         marker_start = "<!-- OCR_EXTRACT_START -->"
216:         marker_end = "<!-- OCR_EXTRACT_END -->"
217: 
218:         extract_section = f"""
219: {marker_start}
220: ## 📝 Texto Extraído (OCR)
221: 
222: > [!info] Método: {method}
223: > Extraído automaticamente pelo OpenCode OCR Pipeline
224: 
225: {text[:5000]}{"..." if len(text) > 5000 else ""}
226: 
227: {marker_end}"""
228: 
229:         if marker_start in content:
230:             # Substituir seção existente
231:             start_idx = content.index(marker_start)
232:             end_idx = content.index(marker_end) + len(marker_end)
233:             content = content[:start_idx] + extract_section + content[end_idx:]
234:         else:
235:             # Adicionar ao final
236:             content += extract_section
237: 
238:         md_file.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
239:     except Exception as e:
240:         log(f"Erro ao atualizar {md_file}: {e}", "WARN")
241: 
242: 
243: def build_index():
244:     """Constrói índice JSON de todas as extrações."""
245:     index = {
246:         "version": "1.0",
247:         "last_updated": datetime.now().isoformat(),
248:         "vault_path": str(VAULT_PATH),
249:         "source_path": str(SOURCE_PATH),
250:         "files": {},
251:         "stats": {
252:             "total_files": 0,
253:             "extracted": 0,
254:             "failed": 0,
255:             "by_method": {}
256:         }
257:     }
258: 
259:     # Listar todos os arquivos processáveis
260:     source_dir = VAULT_PATH / "textos, pdf e esquemas"
261:     files_to_process = []
262: 
263:     for root, dirs, files in os.walk(source_dir):
264:         # Pular diretório de extrações
265:         if ".ocr-extracts" in root:
266:             continue
267:         for fname in files:
268:             fpath = Path(root) / fname
269:             if fpath.suffix.lower() in ALL_EXTS:
270:                 files_to_process.append(fpath)
271: 
272:     log(f"Encontrados {len(files_to_process)} arquivos para indexar")
273: 
274:     # Processar arquivos
275:     for i, fpath in enumerate(files_to_process):
276:         rel = fpath.relative_to(source_dir)
277: 
278:         # Verificar se já foi processado (hash)
279:         extract_file = EXTRACTS_DIR / rel.with_suffix(".extracted.txt")
280:         if extract_file.exists():
281:             # Ler extração existente
282:             try:
283:                 text = extract_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
284:                 index["files"][str(rel)] = {
285:                     "path": str(rel),
286:                     "method": "cached",
287:                     "text_length": len(text),
288:                     "preview": text[:500],
289:                     "has_text": True
290:                 }
291:                 index["stats"]["extracted"] += 1
292:                 method = "cached"
293:                 index["stats"]["by_method"][method] = index["stats"]["by_method"].get(method, 0) + 1
294:             except Exception:
295:                 pass
296:         else:
297:             # Processar novo arquivo
298:             result = process_file(fpath)
299:             index["files"][str(rel)] = result
300:             if result["has_text"]:
301:                 index["stats"]["extracted"] += 1
302:                 method = result["method"]
303:                 index["stats"]["by_method"][method] = index["stats"]["by_method"].get(method, 0) + 1
304:             else:
305:                 index["stats"]["failed"] += 1
306: 
307:         index["stats"]["total_files"] += 1
308: 
309:         if (i + 1) % 50 == 0:
310:             log(f"Progresso: {i + 1}/{len(files_to_process)}")
311: 
312:     # Salvar índice
313:     EXTRACTS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
314:     with open(INDEX_FILE, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
315:         json.dump(index, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
316: 
317:     log(f"Índice salvo: {INDEX_FILE}")
318:     log(f"Total: {index['stats']['total_files']} arquivos, "
319:         f"{index['stats']['extracted']} extraídos, "
320:         f"{index['stats']['failed']} falharam")
321:     log(f"Métodos: {index['stats']['by_method']}")
322: 
323:     return index
324: 
325: 
326: def search_index(query, limit=20):
327:     """Busca texto no índice de extrações."""
328:     if not INDEX_FILE.exists():
329:         log("Índice não existe. Execute --rebuild primeiro.", "ERROR")
330:         return []
331: 
332:     with open(INDEX_FILE, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
333:         index = json.load(f)
334: 
335:     results = []
336:     query_lower = query.lower()
337: 
338:     for path, data in index.get("files", {}).items():
339:         preview = data.get("preview", "").lower()
340:         if query_lower in preview:
341:             results.append({
342:                 "path": path,
343:                 "preview": data["preview"][:300],
344:                 "text_length": data.get("text_length", 0),
345:                 "score": preview.count(query_lower)
346:             })
347: 
348:     # Ordenar por relevância
349:     results.sort(key=lambda x: x["score"], reverse=True)
350:     return results[:limit]
351: 
352: 
353: def extract_single(filepath):
354:     """Extrai texto de um único arquivo e retorna resultado."""
355:     result = process_file(Path(filepath))
356:     if result["has_text"]:
357:         log(f"Extraído: {result['path']} ({result['text_length']} chars, método: {result['method']})")
358:         print(f"\n{'='*60}")
359:         print(f"ARQUIVO: {result['path']}")
360:         print(f"MÉTODO: {result['method']}")
361:         print(f"TAMANHO: {result['text_length']} caracteres")
362:         print(f"{'='*60}")
363:         print(result["preview"])
364:     else:
365:         log(f"Sem texto: {result['path']}", "WARN")
366:     return result
367: 
368: 
369: def main():
370:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="OCR Pipeline para OpenCode")
371:     parser.add_argument("--file", "-f", help="Processar arquivo específico")
372:     parser.add_argument("--query", "-q", help="Buscar no índice de extrações")
373:     parser.add_argument("--rebuild", "-r", action="store_true", help="Reconstruir índice completo")
374:     parser.add_argument("--limit", "-l", type=int, default=20, help="Limite de resultados na busca")
375:     parser.add_argument("--stats", "-s", action="store_true", help="Mostrar estatísticas do índice")
376: 
377:     args = parser.parse_args()
378: 
379:     if args.file:
380:         extract_single(args.file)
381:     elif args.query:
382:         results = search_index(args.query, args.limit)
383:         if results:
384:             print(f"\n🔍 {len(results)} resultados para '{args.query}':\n")
385:             for r in results:
386:                 print(f"  📄 {r['path']} ({r['text_length']} chars, score: {r['score']})")
387:                 print(f"     {r['preview'][:200]}...")
388:                 print()
389:         else:
390:             print(f"Nenhum resultado para '{args.query}'")
391:     elif args.rebuild:
392:         log("=== Reconstruindo índice OCR ===")
393:         build_index()
394:     elif args.stats:
395:         if INDEX_FILE.exists():
396:             with open(INDEX_FILE, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
397:                 index = json.load(f)
398:             stats = index.get("stats", {})
399:             print(f"\n📊 Estatísticas OCR:")
400:             print(f"   Total: {stats.get('total_files', 0)} arquivos")
401:             print(f"   Extraídos: {stats.get('extracted', 0)}")
402:             print(f"   Falharam: {stats.get('failed', 0)}")
403:             print(f"   Métodos: {json.dumps(stats.get('by_method', {}), indent=2)}")
404:         else:
405:             print("Índice não existe. Execute --rebuild primeiro.")
406:     else:
407:         # Modo padrão: extrair tudo
408:         log("=== Iniciando extração OCR completa ===")
409:         build_index()
410: 
411: 
412: if __name__ == "__main__":

7: #   file <arquivo>  - Extrai texto de um arquivo específico
8: #   search <texto>  - Busca no índice de extrações
9: #   stats           - Mostra estatísticas

75: "

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # ============================================================
3: # opencode-maintain.sh
4: # Mantém os symlinks do OpenCode em /mnt/dados/opencode/
5: # Uso: opencode-maintain [status|fix|vacuum|clean|all]
6: # ============================================================
7: set -euo pipefail
8: 
9: DADOS="/mnt/dados/opencode"
10: HOME_DIR="/home/johncoffee"
11: 
12: GREEN='\033[0;32m'
13: RED='\033[0;31m'
14: YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
15: NC='\033[0m'
16: 
17: check_symlinks() {
18:     echo "┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐"
19:     echo "│ Verificando symlinks do OpenCode...         │"
20:     echo "└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘"
21:     local all_ok=true
22: 
23:     for entry in \
24:         "$DADOS:$HOME_DIR/.opencode:.opencode → $DADOS" \
25:         "$DADOS/omo:$HOME_DIR/.omo:.omo → $DADOS/omo" \
26:         "$DADOS/config:$HOME_DIR/.config/opencode:.config/opencode → $DADOS/config" \
27:         "$DADOS/claude:$HOME_DIR/.claude:.claude → $DADOS/claude" \
28:         "$DADOS/share-data:$HOME_DIR/.local/share/opencode:.local/share/opencode → $DADOS/share-data" \
29:         "$DADOS/share-data.old:$HOME_DIR/.local/share/opencode.old:.local/share/opencode.old → $DADOS/share-data.old"
30:     do
31:         IFS=':' read -r target link name <<< "$entry"
32:         if [ -L "$link" ] && [ "$(readlink "$link")" = "$target" ]; then
33:             echo -e "  ${GREEN}✅${NC} $name"
34:         else
35:             echo -e "  ${RED}❌${NC} $name"
36:             all_ok=false
37:         fi
38:     done
39: 
40:     echo ""
41:     if $all_ok; then
42:         echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓ Todos os symlinks estão ok${NC}"
43:     else
44:         echo -e "  ${RED}✗ Alguns symlinks precisam ser reparados${NC}"
45:     fi
46:     echo ""
47:     $all_ok
48: }
49: 
50: fix_symlinks() {
51:     echo "┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐"
52:     echo "│ Reparando symlinks do OpenCode...           │"
53:     echo "└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘"
54: 
55:     for entry in \
56:         "$DADOS:$HOME_DIR/.opencode:.opencode" \
57:         "$DADOS/omo:$HOME_DIR/.omo:.omo" \
58:         "$DADOS/config:$HOME_DIR/.config/opencode:.config/opencode" \
59:         "$DADOS/claude:$HOME_DIR/.claude:.claude" \
60:         "$DADOS/share-data:$HOME_DIR/.local/share/opencode:.local/share/opencode" \
61:         "$DADOS/share-data.old:$HOME_DIR/.local/share/opencode.old:.local/share/opencode.old"
62:     do
63:         IFS=':' read -r target link name <<< "$entry"
64: 
65:         # Remove se existir como diretório real (não symlink)
66:         if [ -d "$link" ] && [ ! -L "$link" ]; then
67:             echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠  $name é diretório real — movendo para backup...${NC}"
68:             mv "$link" "${link}.bak.$(date +%s)"
69:         fi
70: 
71:         # Remove symlink quebrado
72:         if [ -L "$link" ] && [ ! -e "$link" ]; then
73:             echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠  Symlink quebrado: $name${NC}"
74:             rm "$link"
75:         fi
76: 
77:         # Garante que o diretório pai existe
78:         parent_dir=$(dirname "$link")
79:         mkdir -p "$parent_dir"
80: 
81:         # Cria o symlink se não existir
82:         if [ ! -e "$link" ]; then
83:             ln -s "$target" "$link"
84:             echo -e "  ${GREEN}✅ Criado: $name → $target${NC}"
85:         fi
86:     done
87:     echo ""
88: }
89: 
90: vacuum_db() {
91:     local DB="$DADOS/share-data/opencode.db"
92:     if [ ! -f "$DB" ]; then
93:         echo -e "${YELLOW}Banco não encontrado em $DB${NC}"
94:         return 1
95:     fi
96: 
97:     if pgrep -x "opencode" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
98:         echo -e "${RED}OpenCode está rodando. Feche antes de compactar.${NC}"
99:         return 1
100:     fi
101: 
102:     echo "┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐"
103:     echo "│ Compactando opencode.db...                  │"
104:     echo "└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘"
105:     local before=$(du -h "$DB" | cut -f1)
106:     echo -e "  Antes: ${YELLOW}$before${NC}"
107: 
108:     echo "  Verificando integridade..."
109:     sqlite3 "$DB" "PRAGMA integrity_check;"
110:     echo "  Compactando (VACUUM)..."
111:     sqlite3 "$DB" "VACUUM;"
112:     echo "  Checkpoint WAL..."
113:     sqlite3 "$DB" "PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);"
114: 
115:     local after=$(du -h "$DB" | cut -f1)
116:     echo -e "  Depois: ${GREEN}$after${NC}"
117:     echo ""
118: }
119: 
120: clean_sessions() {
121:     echo "┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐"
122:     echo "│ Limpando continuations antigas...           │"
123:     echo "└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘"
124:     local count=0
125:     if [ -d "$DADOS/omo/run-continuation" ]; then
126:         count=$(find "$DADOS/omo/run-continuation" -name "*.json" -mtime +30 | wc -l)
127:         find "$DADOS/omo/run-continuation" -name "*.json" -mtime +30 -delete 2>/dev/null
128:         echo -e "  ${GREEN}🗑  $count continuations antigas (+30d) removidas${NC}"
129:     fi
130:     echo ""
131: }
132: 
133: show_usage() {
134:     echo "Uso: $0 [comando]"
135:     echo "  status     - Verifica symlinks"
136:     echo "  fix        - Repara symlinks quebrados"
137:     echo "  vacuum     - Compacta opencode.db (fechar opencode antes)"
138:     echo "  clean      - Remove continuations antigas (+30d)"
139:     echo "  all        - Executa tudo (fix + vacuum + clean)"
140:     echo ""
141:     echo "Sem argumento: executa status"
142: }
143:
