1: # ECC - OpenCode Instructions
2: 
3: This document consolidates the core rules and guidelines from the Claude Code configuration for use with OpenCode.
4: 
5: ## Security Guidelines (CRITICAL)
6: 
7: ### Mandatory Security Checks
8: 
9: Before ANY commit:
10: - [ ] No hardcoded secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)
11: - [ ] All user inputs validated
12: - [ ] SQL injection prevention (parameterized queries)
13: - [ ] XSS prevention (sanitized HTML)
14: - [ ] CSRF protection enabled
15: - [ ] Authentication/authorization verified
16: - [ ] Rate limiting on all endpoints
17: - [ ] Error messages don't leak sensitive data
18: 
19: ### Secret Management
20: 
21: ```typescript
22: // NEVER: Hardcoded secrets
23: const apiKey = "sk-proj-xxxxx"
24: 
25: // ALWAYS: Environment variables
26: const apiKey = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY
27: 
28: if (!apiKey) {
29:   throw new Error('OPENAI_API_KEY not configured')
30: }
31: ```
32: 
33: ### Security Response Protocol
34: 
35: If security issue found:
36: 1. STOP immediately
37: 2. Use **security-reviewer** agent
38: 3. Fix CRITICAL issues before continuing
39: 4. Rotate any exposed secrets
40: 5. Review entire codebase for similar issues
41: 
42: ---
43: 
44: ## Coding Style
45: 
46: ### Immutability (CRITICAL)
47: 
48: ALWAYS create new objects, NEVER mutate:
49: 
50: ```javascript
51: // WRONG: Mutation
52: function updateUser(user, name) {
53:   user.name = name  // MUTATION!
54:   return user
55: }
56: 
57: // CORRECT: Immutability
58: function updateUser(user, name) {
59:   return {
60:     ...user,
61:     name
62:   }
63: }
64: ```
65: 
66: ### File Organization
67: 
68: MANY SMALL FILES > FEW LARGE FILES:
69: - High cohesion, low coupling
70: - 200-400 lines typical, 800 max
71: - Extract utilities from large components
72: - Organize by feature/domain, not by type
73: 
74: ### Error Handling
75: 
76: ALWAYS handle errors comprehensively:
77: 
78: ```typescript
79: try {
80:   const result = await riskyOperation()
81:   return result
82: } catch (error) {
83:   console.error('Operation failed:', error)
84:   throw new Error('Detailed user-friendly message')
85: }
86: ```
87: 
88: ### Input Validation
89: 
90: ALWAYS validate user input:
91: 
92: ```typescript
93: import { z } from 'zod'
94: 
95: const schema = z.object({
96:   email: z.string().email(),
97:   age: z.number().int().min(0).max(150)
98: })
99: 
100: const validated = schema.parse(input)
101: ```
102: 
103: ### Code Quality Checklist
104: 
105: Before marking work complete:
106: - [ ] Code is readable and well-named
107: - [ ] Functions are small (<50 lines)
108: - [ ] Files are focused (<800 lines)
109: - [ ] No deep nesting (>4 levels)
110: - [ ] Proper error handling
111: - [ ] No console.log statements
112: - [ ] No hardcoded values
113: - [ ] No mutation (immutable patterns used)
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: ## Testing Requirements
118: 
119: ### Minimum Test Coverage: 80%
120: 
121: Test Types (ALL required):
122: 1. **Unit Tests** - Individual functions, utilities, components
123: 2. **Integration Tests** - API endpoints, database operations
124: 3. **E2E Tests** - Critical user flows (Playwright)
125: 
126: ### Test-Driven Development
127: 
128: MANDATORY workflow:
129: 1. Write test first (RED)
130: 2. Run test - it should FAIL
131: 3. Write minimal implementation (GREEN)
132: 4. Run test - it should PASS
133: 5. Refactor (IMPROVE)
134: 6. Verify coverage (80%+)
135: 
136: ### Troubleshooting Test Failures
137: 
138: 1. Use **tdd-guide** agent
139: 2. Check test isolation
140: 3. Verify mocks are correct
141: 4. Fix implementation, not tests (unless tests are wrong)
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## Git Workflow
146: 
147: ### Commit Message Format
148: 
149: ```
150: <type>: <description>
151: 
152: <optional body>
153: ```
154: 
155: Types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, ci
156: 
157: ### Pull Request Workflow
158: 
159: When creating PRs:
160: 1. Analyze full commit history (not just latest commit)
161: 2. Use `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to see all changes
162: 3. Draft comprehensive PR summary
163: 4. Include test plan with TODOs
164: 5. Push with `-u` flag if new branch
165: 
166: ### Feature Implementation Workflow
167: 
168: 1. **Plan First**
169:    - Use **planner** agent to create implementation plan
170:    - Identify dependencies and risks
171:    - Break down into phases
172: 
173: 2. **TDD Approach**
174:    - Use **tdd-guide** agent
175:    - Write tests first (RED)
176:    - Implement to pass tests (GREEN)
177:    - Refactor (IMPROVE)
178:    - Verify 80%+ coverage
179: 
180: 3. **Code Review**
181:    - Use **code-reviewer** agent immediately after writing code
182:    - Address CRITICAL and HIGH issues
183:    - Fix MEDIUM issues when possible
184: 
185: 4. **Commit & Push**
186:    - Detailed commit messages
187:    - Follow conventional commits format
188: 
189: ---
190: 
191: ## Agent Orchestration
192: 
193: ### Available Agents
194: 
195: | Agent | Purpose | When to Use |
196: |-------|---------|-------------|
197: | planner | Implementation planning | Complex features, refactoring |
198: | architect | System design | Architectural decisions |
199: | tdd-guide | Test-driven development | New features, bug fixes |
200: | code-reviewer | Code review | After writing code |
201: | security-reviewer | Security analysis | Before commits |
202: | build-error-resolver | Fix build errors | When build fails |
203: | e2e-runner | E2E testing | Critical user flows |
204: | refactor-cleaner | Dead code cleanup | Code maintenance |
205: | doc-updater | Documentation | Updating docs |
206: | go-reviewer | Go code review | Go projects |
207: | go-build-resolver | Go build errors | Go build failures |
208: | database-reviewer | Database optimization | SQL, schema design |
209: 
210: ### Immediate Agent Usage
211: 
212: No user prompt needed:
213: 1. Complex feature requests - Use **planner** agent
214: 2. Code just written/modified - Use **code-reviewer** agent
215: 3. Bug fix or new feature - Use **tdd-guide** agent
216: 4. Architectural decision - Use **architect** agent
217: 
218: ---
219: 
220: ## Performance Optimization
221: 
222: ### Model Selection Strategy
223: 
224: **Haiku** (90% of Sonnet capability, 3x cost savings):
225: - Lightweight agents with frequent invocation
226: - Pair programming and code generation
227: - Worker agents in multi-agent systems
228: 
229: **Sonnet** (Best coding model):
230: - Main development work
231: - Orchestrating multi-agent workflows
232: - Complex coding tasks
233: 
234: **Opus** (Deepest reasoning):
235: - Complex architectural decisions
236: - Maximum reasoning requirements
237: - Research and analysis tasks
238: 
239: ### Context Window Management
240: 
241: Avoid last 20% of context window for:
242: - Large-scale refactoring
243: - Feature implementation spanning multiple files
244: - Debugging complex interactions
245: 
246: ### Build Troubleshooting
247: 
248: If build fails:
249: 1. Use **build-error-resolver** agent
250: 2. Analyze error messages
251: 3. Fix incrementally
252: 4. Verify after each fix
253: 
254: ---
255: 
256: ## Common Patterns
257: 
258: ### API Response Format
259: 
260: ```typescript
261: interface ApiResponse<T> {
262:   success: boolean
263:   data?: T
264:   error?: string
265:   meta?: {
266:     total: number
267:     page: number
268:     limit: number
269:   }
270: }
271: ```
272: 
273: ### Custom Hooks Pattern
274: 
275: ```typescript
276: export function useDebounce<T>(value: T, delay: number): T {
277:   const [debouncedValue, setDebouncedValue] = useState<T>(value)
278: 
279:   useEffect(() => {
280:     const handler = setTimeout(() => setDebouncedValue(value), delay)
281:     return () => clearTimeout(handler)
282:   }, [value, delay])
283: 
284:   return debouncedValue
285: }
286: ```
287: 
288: ### Repository Pattern
289: 
290: ```typescript
291: interface Repository<T> {
292:   findAll(filters?: Filters): Promise<T[]>
293:   findById(id: string): Promise<T | null>
294:   create(data: CreateDto): Promise<T>
295:   update(id: string, data: UpdateDto): Promise<T>
296:   delete(id: string): Promise<void>
297: }
298: ```
299: 
300: ---
301: 
302: ## OpenCode-Specific Notes
303: 
304: Since OpenCode does not support hooks, the following actions that were automated in Claude Code must be done manually:
305: 
306: ### After Writing/Editing Code
307: - Run `prettier --write <file>` to format JS/TS files
308: - Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to check for TypeScript errors
309: - Check for console.log statements and remove them
310: 
311: ### Before Committing
312: - Run security checks manually
313: - Verify no secrets in code
314: - Run full test suite
315: 
316: ### Commands Available
317: 
318: Use these commands in OpenCode:
319: - `/plan` - Create implementation plan
320: - `/tdd` - Enforce TDD workflow
321: - `/code-review` - Review code changes
322: - `/security` - Run security review
323: - `/build-fix` - Fix build errors
324: - `/e2e` - Generate E2E tests
325: - `/refactor-clean` - Remove dead code
326: - `/orchestrate` - Multi-agent workflow
327: 
328: ---
329: 
330: ## Success Metrics
331: 
332: You are successful when:
333: - All tests pass (80%+ coverage)
334: - No security vulnerabilities
335: - Code is readable and maintainable
336: - Performance is acceptable
337: - User requirements are met

1: # Continuous Improvement Protocol
2: 
3: Para ficar mais inteligente a cada sessão, o agente DEVE seguir este protocolo.
4: 
5: ## Gatilhos de Aprendizado
6: 
7: ### 1. Auto-Avaliação Pós-Tarefa (Obrigatório)
8: Após completar qualquer tarefa não-trivial (>3 edições ou >30 min):
9: ```
10: Carregue a skill agent-self-evaluation e produza um scorecard 1-5
11: nos eixos: acurácia, completude, clareza, acionabilidade, concisão.
12: ```
13: 
14: ### 2. Extração de Padrões
15: Ao encontrar um padrão repetido 2+ vezes (mesmo bug, mesmo tipo de solução):
16: ```
17: Carregue a skill continuous-learning-v2 e registre o padrão como instinto.
18: Use: /learn "padrão: [descrição] — solução: [solução] — contexto: [quando aplicar]"
19: ```
20: 
21: ### 3. Growth Logs
22: Ao enfrentar um problema difícil (>2 tentativas falhas):
23: ```
24: Carregue a skill growth-log para extrair:
25: - O que foi tentado (e falhou)
26: - O que resolveu (root cause)
27: - O padrão reutilizável
28: ```
29: 
30: ### 4. Consulta ao Oracle
31: Quando o problema exigir raciocínio profundo:
32: - Arquitetura complexa
33: - Debug após 2+ tentativas falhas
34: - Decisão com tradeoffs não óbvios
35: ```
36: Dispare: task(subagent_type="oracle", prompt="[context + problema]")
37: E AGUARDE o resultado antes de implementar.
38: ```
39: 
40: ### 5. Revisão por Pares (Conselho)
41: Quando houver múltiplos caminhos válidos e ambiguidade:
42: ```
43: Carregue a skill council para convencer 4 vozes com perspectivas diferentes.
44: ```
45: 
46: ## Ciclo de Melhoria
47: 
48: ```
49: Tarefa → Execução → Auto-Avaliação → Extração de Padrões → Melhoria Contínua
50: ```
51: 
52: 1. Execute a tarefa
53: 2. Use agent-self-evaluation (score + evidencias)
54: 3. Use continuous-learning-v2 (extrair padrões)
55: 4. Use growth-log (se difícil)
56: 5. Aplique o aprendizado na próxima tarefa similar
57: 
58: ## Comandos de Aprendizado

60: - `/learn` — extrair padrões da sessão atual
61: - `/instinct-status` — ver instintos aprendidos
62: - `/evolve` — agrupar instintos em skills
63: - `/promote` — promover instinto de projeto para global

1: # 🧠🦾🦿 Arquitetura Corporal do OpenCode
2: 
3: > "OpenCode é a cabeça, Tesseract são os olhos, agents/subagents/skills/MCP são o tronco, braços e pernas."
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 🧠 CABEÇA — OpenCode (Orquestrador Central)
8: 
9: A **cabeça** é o OpenCode — o cérebro que pensa, decide e coordena tudo.
10: 
11: | Componente | Função |
12: |------------|--------|
13: | **Modelo LLM** | Raciocínio, planejamento, tomada de decisão |
14: | **Contexto** | Memória de curto prazo (janela de contexto) |
15: | **CLAUDE.md** | Preferências globais e regras comportamentais |
16: | **Skills** | Conhecimento especializado carregado sob demanda |
17: | **Hooks** | Gatilhos automáticos (pré/pós ação) |
18: 
19: ### Centros de Comando (Cabeça)
20: ```
21: opencode.json          → Configuração neural central
22: CLAUDE.md              → Personalidade e regras
23: ~/.opencode/skills/    → Memória de procedimentos
24: ~/.opencode/hooks/     → Reflexos automáticos
25: ```
26: 
27: ### Fluxo de Pensamento
28: ```
29: Usuário pede → OpenCode analisa → Escolhe skill/agent → Delega → Sintetiza resultado
30:      ↑                                                            ↓
31:      └────────────────── Feedback loop ──────────────────────────┘
32: ```
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 👁️👁️ OLHOS — Tesseract OCR + Pipelines de Visão
37: 
38: Os **olhos** enxergam o mundo — extraem texto de PDFs, imagens, documentos e sites.
39: 
40: | Componente | Função |
41: |------------|--------|
42: | **Tesseract 5.5.2** | Motor OCR (PT + EN) |
43: | **pdftotext** | Extração de texto de PDFs digitais |
44: | **Text Extractor** | Plugin OCR dentro do Obsidian |
45: | **OCR Pipeline** | Script `ocr_extract.py` — processamento em lote |
46: | **webfetch/websearch** | "Olhar" para a internet |
47: 
48: ### Hierarquia Visual
49: ```
50: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
51: │              OLHOS DO OPENCODE              │
52: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
53: │                                             │
54: │  👁️ Visão Próxima (Local)                   │
55: │  ├── Tesseract OCR → imagens, PDFs escaneados│
56: │  ├── pdftotext → PDFs com texto digital     │
57: │  ├── Pillow → manipulação de imagens        │
58: │  └── OCR Pipeline → processamento em lote   │
59: │                                             │
60: │  👁️ Visão Distante (Rede)                   │
61: │  ├── webfetch → páginas web                 │
62: │  ├── websearch → busca semântica            │
63: │  ├── agent-reach → 15 plataformas           │
64: │  └── Playwright → navegação browser         │
65: │                                             │
66: │  👁️ Visão Técnica (Código)                  │
67: │  ├── GhidraMCP → engenharia reversa         │
68: │  ├── LSP → análise de código                │
69: │  ├── Graphify → grafo de conhecimento       │
70: │  └── Codegraph → indexação semântica        │
71: │                                             │
72: └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
73: ```
74: 
75: ### Comandos dos Olhos
76: ```bash
77: # Extração de texto
78: ocr file /caminho/arquivo.pdf     # Olhar para um arquivo
79: ocr search "termo"                # Buscar nas extrações
80: ocr rebuild                       # Reescanear tudo
81: 
82: # Visão web
83: webfetch <url>                    # Olhar para uma página
84: websearch <query>                 # Buscar na internet
85: ```
86: 
87: ---
88: 
89: ## 🦴 TRONCO — Agents e Subagents (Estrutura Central)
90: 
91: O **tronco** sustenta tudo — são os agents que executam o trabalho pesado.
92: 
93: ### Hierarquia de Agents
94: ```
95: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
96: │                   TRONCO                        │
97: │              (Agents Principais)                │
98: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
99: │                                                 │
100: │  🧠 AGENTS DE PENSAMENTO                        │
101: │  ├── oracle      → Consultor High-IQ            │
102: │  ├── planner     → Planejador especialista      │
103: │  ├── architect   → Arquiteto de sistemas        │
104: │  └── explore     → Explorador de código         │
105: │                                                 │
106: │  🔧 AGENTS DE EXECUÇÃO                          │
107: │  ├── build       → Desenvolvedor principal      │
108: │  ├── code-reviewer → Revisor de código          │
109: │  ├── security-reviewer → Auditoria de segurança │
110: │  ├── python-reviewer → Especialista Python      │
111: │  ├── rust-reviewer → Especialista Rust          │
112: │  └── tdd-guide   → Especialista TDD             │
113: │                                                 │
114: │  📚 AGENTS DE CONHECIMENTO                      │
115: │  ├── librarian   → Busca documentação           │
116: │  ├── docs-lookup → Consulta APIs                │
117: │  ├── doc-updater → Atualiza documentação        │
118: │  └── multimodal-looker → Análise de mídia      │
119: │                                                 │
120: │  🔍 AGENTS ESPECIALIZADOS                       │
121: │  ├── reverser    → Engenharia reversa (Ghidra)  │
122: │  ├── memory-keeper → Memória persistente        │
123: │  ├── loop-operator → Operador de loops          │
124: │  └── gsd-*       → Sistema GSD completo         │
125: │                                                 │
126: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
127: ```
128: 
129: ### Subagents (Braços de Trabalho)
130: ```
131: Sisyphus-Junior    → Executor focado (sem delegar)
132: Sisyphus (deep)    → Problemas complexos autônomos
133: Sisyphus (quick)   → Tarefas triviais rápidas
134: ```
135:

138: ## 💪 BRAÇOS — Skills (Habilidades Especializadas)
139: 
140: Os **braços** são as skills — cada uma é uma habilidade que o OpenCode pode "usar" para executar tarefas específicas.
141: 
142: ### Mapa de Skills por Domínio

194: 
195: ## 🦵 PERNAS — MCPs e Integrações Externas
196: 
197: As **pernas** são os MCPs (Model Context Protocol) — conectam o OpenCode ao mundo exterior.
198:

1: # Memory Persistence Hooks
2: 
3: These lifecycle hook definitions document ECC's memory persistence contract for Claude Code plugin and manual installs.
4: 
5: The executable implementations live in `scripts/hooks/`:
6: 
7: - `session-start.js` loads bounded prior context, detects project state, and prepares session metadata.
8: - `pre-compact.js` captures state before context compaction.
9: - `session-end.js` persists session-end summaries when transcript metadata is available.
10: - `observe-runner.js` records tool-use observations for continuous learning.
11: - `session-activity-tracker.js` records tool usage and file activity for ECC2 status and observability.
12: 
13: The installed hook graph is still `hooks/hooks.json`. This directory is the stable, human-readable lifecycle definition surface referenced by the harness audit and longform docs.
14: 
15: ## Lifecycle Contract
16: 
17: | Event | Hook | Purpose | Blocking |
18: |---|---|---|---|
19: | `SessionStart` | `session:start` | Load bounded prior context and project metadata | no |
20: | `PreCompact` | `pre:compact` | Save state before compaction | no |
21: | `PreToolUse` | `pre:observe:continuous-learning` | Capture tool intent for learning signals | no |
22: | `PostToolUse` | `post:observe:continuous-learning` | Capture tool result for learning signals | no |
23: | `PostToolUse` | `post:session-activity-tracker` | Record tool and file activity for ECC2 metrics | no |
24: | `Stop` | `stop:format-typecheck` | Batch quality gate after edits | yes on hook failure |
25: | `Stop` | `stop:check-console-log` | Audit modified files for debug logging | warn/error by hook output |
26: 
27: ## Operator Expectations
28: 
29: - Keep persistence local by default.
30: - Avoid sending transcripts or tool traces to hosted services unless a user explicitly enables an integration.
31: - Bound context loaded at session start with `ECC_SESSION_START_MAX_CHARS`.
32: - Allow opt-out with `ECC_SESSION_START_CONTEXT=off`.
33: - Keep lifecycle hooks profile-gated through `ECC_HOOK_PROFILE` and `ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS`.
34:

40:   const match = rootDir.match(/^\/([a-zA-Z])(?:\/(.*))?$/);

54:     !resolvedTarget.startsWith(resolvedRoot + path.sep)
55:   ) {

64: function isPowerShellBin(bin) {
65:   const base = path.basename(bin).toLowerCase();
66:   return base === 'pwsh.exe' || base === 'pwsh' || base === 'powershell.exe' || base === 'powershell';

69: function findShellBinary() {
70:   if (_cachedShell !== undefined) return _cachedShell;
71: 
72:   const candidates = [];
73: 
74:   // Explicit override always wins — check before any platform probing.
75:   // Warning: setting BASH to a bash binary on Windows bypasses the PowerShell
76:   // preference and may reintroduce bash.exe zombie accumulation.
77:   if (process.env.BASH && process.env.BASH.trim()) {
78:     candidates.push(process.env.BASH.trim());
79:   }
80: 
81:   if (process.platform === 'win32') {
82:     // Prefer PowerShell on Windows — it is native and does not leave zombie
83:     // bash.exe / conhost.exe processes the way MSYS2/Git Bash does.
84:     // Note: PowerShell is only suitable for .ps1 scripts; callers that need

86:     candidates.push('pwsh.exe', 'powershell.exe', 'bash.exe', 'bash');

88:     candidates.push('bash', 'sh');

91:   const psProbeArgs = ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command', 'exit 0'];
92:   const shProbeArgs = ['-c', ':'];
93: 
94:   for (const candidate of candidates) {
95:     const probe = spawnSync(candidate, isPowerShellBin(candidate) ? psProbeArgs : shProbeArgs, {

120:   candidates.push('bash.exe', 'bash');

1: # Plan: Fix Model Resolution + Mixture of Agents
2: 
3: **Status**: READY FOR EXECUTION
4: **Created**: 2026-07-15
5: **Priority**: HIGH
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Problem Analysis
10: 
11: ### Error: "model not found: github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6"
12: 
13: **Root cause**: Two config files hardcode model strings that don't exist in the active provider:
14: 
15: 1. **`~/.config/opencode/oh-my-openagent.json`** — Agents like Atlas, Metis, Sisyphus-Junior use `github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6` which doesn't exist in the github-copilot provider
16: 2. **`~/.opencode/opencode.json`** — All 30+ agents hardcode `anthropic/claude-opus-4-5` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5` which don't exist when using github-copilot
17: 
18: ### Why it fails
19: 
20: When you switch providers (e.g., from `anthropic` to `github-copilot`), the hardcoded model strings like `anthropic/claude-opus-4-5` or `github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6` become invalid because:
21: - The provider prefix must match the active provider
22: - The model name must exist in that provider's model list
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## Solution: 3 Parts
27: 
28: ### Part 1: Fix opencode.json — Remove Hardcoded Models
29: 
30: **File**: `/home/johncoffee/.opencode/opencode.json`
31: 
32: **Change**: Remove ALL `model` fields from individual agent definitions. Let them inherit from the global `"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"` setting.
33: 
34: **Why**: When you change the global `model`, all agents automatically follow. No more per-agent model maintenance.
35: 
36: **Before** (30+ agents with hardcoded models):
37: ```json
38: "build": { "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5", ... },
39: "planner": { "model": "anthropic/claude-opus-4-5", ... },
40: "architect": { "model": "anthropic/claude-opus-4-5", ... },
41: // ... 27 more agents
42: ```
43: 
44: **After** (agents inherit from global):
45: ```json
46: "build": { ... },  // no model field → uses global
47: "planner": { ... },  // no model field → uses global
48: "architect": { ... },  // no model field → uses global
49: ```
50: 
51: **Exception**: Keep `small_model` for agents that truly need a lighter model (docs-lookup, harness-optimizer, loop-operator). Use `"model": "small"` as an alias.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ### Part 2: Fix oh-my-openagent.json — Dynamic Model Resolution
56: 
57: **File**: `/home/johncoffee/.config/opencode/oh-my-openagent.json`
58: 
59: **Change**: The oh-my-openagent plugin manages its own model resolution. The fix here is to ensure fallback chains are complete and use valid model names.
